entries.title: Validated release metadata and quiet automatic version checks
entries.what: Release lookup validates both the transport endpoint and returned package identity. Automatic checks quietly suppress failures while explicit lookup can return errors to the invoking command.
entries.mechanism:
Release lookup accepts valid metadata from the running package's registry endpoint or an explicitly configured operator endpoint. Automatic notices require a newer version, and their quiet failure policy differs from direct lookup.

comparePackageVersions trims both strings and uses semver.valid/compare only when both are valid; otherwise it returns undefined. isNewerPackageVersion uses positive semantic comparison when available, but falls back to inequality of trimmed strings when either version is invalid. getLatestIceRelease first returns undefined for any truthy getIceEnv('ICE_OFFLINE') value, including strings '0' or 'false'; this is broader than the CLI's true/1/yes parser. Its default URL is https://registry.npmjs.org/<encodeURIComponent(PACKAGE_NAME)>/latest. process.env.ICE_UPDATE_URL overrides only when truthy. new URL errors propagate. HTTPS is required except HTTP is allowed for hostname exactly localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]; username/password are rejected, and redirect:'error' prevents redirects. Fetch uses accept:application/json, AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs??10000), and getIceUserAgent(currentVersion) (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/version-check.ts:7-53).

Non-OK HTTP returns undefined. Parsed metadata must be a non-null non-array object with a trimmed valid semantic-version string. packageName??name may be omitted, otherwise must be a string whose trimmed nonempty value matches the scoped/unscoped package grammar; blank means absent. The default endpoint rejects a different package identity, while an explicitly configured endpoint can hand off to another valid package. note is included only as a trimmed nonempty string. Fetch/JSON/URL errors are not caught in getLatestIceRelease; getLatestIceVersion projects version. checkForNewIceVersion separately skips any truthy ICE_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK, catches all lookup/comparison failures and returns only a newer release. Direct lookup ignores ICE_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK. No disk cache, retry, redirect fallback or network attempt is intrinsic to the helper (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/version-check.ts:54-84).

The user agent is exactly ice/<version> (<process.platform>; <bun/version or node/process.version>; <process.arch>), with Bun selected by truthy process.versions.bun. The tests specify package identity, operator handoff, release note trimming, prerelease comparison, non-aliasing of PI_* variables, direct-versus-automatic disable behavior and rejected endpoint shapes; they were read only.
entries.dependency_text: CLI-038 owns explicit self-update command sequencing and SET-002 its installation command selection. CLI-042 owns the existing native startup cache/notices; do not count those as missing here.
entries.rust: Rust startup lookup uses crates.io ice-cli metadata, request timeout 1800 ms and user agent icers/<VERSION>. It distinguishes missing(404/410) from transient HTTP/JSON failures and reads crate.max_version. Its semantic comparison strips leading 'v' characters after trim, uses cmp_precedence, and returns false if either parse fails. Its disable controls are native offline_env_enabled and presence of ICERS_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK, rather than the two TS truthy helpers (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:17-21; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:119-158; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:445-480). CLI-042 credits native caching, and CLI-043/045 own native release/install sources. No equivalent operator-controlled npm package handoff or TS structured note is present at this registry boundary.
entries.port: Keep the native crates.io distribution source and existing cache. Define explicit accepted native/TS-compatible environment names, endpoint validation and direct-versus-quiet error contracts; add an operator metadata adapter only where package handoff is a supported distribution feature. Preserve semantic prerelease ordering and document invalid-version handling rather than blindly treating arbitrary unequal strings as upgrades. Test future endpoint validation, package identity, exact off/skip controls and failure/cache interaction without running them in this audit.
entries.priority_reason: Update notices and explicit update commands need consistent metadata and opt-out semantics without confusing native package distribution with npm.

entries.title: Windows loaded dependency quarantine and deferred cleanup
entries.what: The TS npm self-update path moves loaded native dependencies aside so package replacement can proceed while the process is alive. Native executable activation has its own staged helper and does not require reproducing Node's module inventory.
entries.mechanism:
Loaded native files are quarantined under the nearest node_modules directory before a TS package self-update. Later startup attempts best-effort removal of that quarantine, while individual moves preserve a copy at the original package location.

normalizePath applies resolve then toNamespacedPath. getQuarantineRoot walks upward from the package directory until basename lowercased equals node_modules, returning <node_modules>/.ice-native-quarantine; reaching the filesystem root returns undefined. getLoadedSharedObjects reads process.report.getReport().sharedObjects, returns [] unless an array, ignores nonstrings, normalizes each path and its package root, compares them lowercased, keeps only getCwdRelativePath-contained files, and deduplicates case-insensitively while returning the normalized original spelling (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/windows-self-update.ts:1-46).

cleanupWindowsSelfUpdateQuarantine returns if no root and recursively force-removes the complete quarantine root, swallowing removal errors. quarantineWindowsNativeDependencies returns if no root or no loaded files; otherwise it creates a unique <Date.now>-<pid>-<randomUUID> run directory. In report order, still-existing loaded files are moved to the same package-relative destination under that run after recursive parent creation, then copied back to the original location. Rename/copy failure propagates; there is no per-file rollback or finally. A failure after rename can therefore leave a moved file without its replacement. This is the source's mutation ordering, not an executed Windows failure (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/windows-self-update.ts:48-84).

The helper itself has no platform guard. Main invokes cleanup only on win32; explicit self-update invocation is CLI-038. No direct helper test was found by the bounded test import/function-name search, so no Windows runtime behavior is claimed.
entries.interfaces: cleanupWindowsSelfUpdateQuarantine(packageDir):void; quarantineWindowsNativeDependencies(packageDir):void. Persistent temporary path: nearest node_modules/.ice-native-quarantine/<timestamp>-<pid>-<uuid>/<package-relative-file>. Runtime inventory: process.report sharedObjects.
entries.dependency_text: CLI-038 owns when TS quarantine runs and handles update command failure; CLI-046 owns native Windows detached activation/status/cleanup. Generic path containment reuses the package worker's paths.ts source credit.
entries.rust: Rust's native helper takes parent/staging/staged-version/target/temp/backup/rollback/status paths, emits status by a temporary file plus move, validates regular nonempty files and MZ header and rejects reparse directories (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:1297-1394). The complete existing staged activation and rollback contract is credited to CLI-046. That executable transaction is a genuine native alternative to process.report-driven Node dependency quarantine.
entries.port: Keep the native staged activation design and avoid adding a node_modules or process.report dependency to Rust. If a supported embedded JS/npm update path needs this helper, preserve its caller guard and containment and make rename/copy rollback explicit. Treat ordinary cleanup failure as best effort; do not let a partial quarantine silently destroy the only usable file.
entries.priority_reason: The TS mechanism is runtime-specific; the native staged executable workflow already addresses the corresponding product need and is counted in CLI.

entries.title: Tool-result image identity, failure policy and post-hook normalization
entries.what: Normalize tool-produced images once before their final history result, including images replaced by extension hooks. Preserve a tool's output and object identity when processing fails or makes no change.
entries.mechanism:
The TS normalizer preserves text/image order and returns the original array when nothing changed. The coding-session caller runs it after extension result hooks, so an extension-injected image receives the same treatment as the tool's own image.

normalizeToolResultImages immediately returns content if no block has type image. autoResizeImages defaults true. It visits blocks sequentially; nonimages retain the same object. Images are decoded with Buffer.from(data,'base64') and passed with their declared MIME to processImage. A failed processing result keeps the original image block and does not set changed. A success with equal data and MIME and zero hints also keeps the original block. Otherwise it appends a fresh {type:'image', data, mimeType}, then one text block containing hints joined by newline when any hints exist, and marks changed. It returns the new array only if changed, otherwise the original. A helper rejection propagates; the explicit fallback applies to the ok:false result, not every thrown error (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tool-result-images.ts:22-62).

AgentSession.afterToolCall first optionally awaits the tool_result extension chain. It selects hookResult?.content??result.content??[], normalizes with the live settings auto-resize flag, returns undefined only when there is no hook result and array identity is unchanged, otherwise returns content plus hook details/usage and hook isError??original isError. Thus injected/replaced images are processed after the last hook. The core result merge, usage preservation and hook patch semantics remain AGENT-015/016 and EXT-025 (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts:648-679).

The direct suite specifies original-array identity for no images, small unchanged images, disabled auto-resize and undecodable images; it also specifies conversion despite disabled resizing, exact hint placement and surrounding text order. These are source assertions, not executed test results.
entries.dependency_text: TOOLS-023 owns MIME, codecs, worker execution and all resize/hint algorithms. This entry owns normalization placement, default propagation, identity and failure disposition. SESSION-019 and CLI-009 retain their separate input/argument admission boundaries.
entries.rust: Rust wraps each active executable tool in ImageTool, which executes it, skips processing if no images, then uses spawn_blocking to call normalize_image_blocks and preserves the other result fields. A completed processing join checks cancellation and can turn the result into 'Image processing cancelled'. normalize_image_blocks decodes strict base64, always calls prepare_inline_image without an auto-resize setting, inserts hints after each image and replaces decode/processing failure with omission text. The inline test explicitly expects omission while retaining details (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/image_tool.rs:30-73; rust:crates/ice-harness/src/image_tool.rs:108-124; rust:crates/ice-tools/src/image_processing.rs:128-154). The wrapper runs before core after_tool_call; that later hook can replace content, and finalize_executed_tool_call performs no second normalization (rust:crates/ice-agent/src/agent_loop.rs:1091-1139). Rust also normalizes user images through a blocking worker at the harness boundary, which credits later preprocessing despite raw CLI attachment ingestion (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:4478-4495).
entries.port: Retain blocking-worker isolation and native result metadata. Apply the chosen image failure policy explicitly, propagate auto-resize settings, and place a final normalizer after extension result patches if TS compatibility is required. Keep untouched content unchanged at the semantic level even where Rust ownership removes JS reference identity. Add future assertions for extension-added images, failed decode with retained original content, disabled resizing, hint ordering and cancellation after worker completion.
entries.priority_reason: A misplaced or differently configured normalizer changes persistent tool output and can leave extension-injected oversized images untreated.

entries.title: Optional clipboard module loading and text-read fallback
entries.what: Clipboard reads must distinguish an empty current clipboard from a failed backend lookup. TS prefers a Wayland text read over a potentially stale native X11 clipboard, while native Rust delegates directly to its optional clipboard library.
entries.mechanism:
The TS native clipboard addon is optional and tried through two module resolution roots. Text reads use a successful empty Wayland response as the authoritative empty clipboard, falling back only when that read failed.

loadClipboardNative tries requires in order, defaulting to createRequire(import.meta.url) then a require rooted at <dirname(process.execPath)>/package.json. It returns the first successful require('@zykairotis/ice-clipboard') cast without runtime shape validation, catches each load failure, and returns null after all failures. The exported clipboard is initialized once at module load only when TERMUX_VERSION is falsy and either platform is not linux or DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY is truthy; calling loadClipboardNative itself bypasses that guard (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard-native.ts:14-33).

readClipboardText first uses wl-paste only when os.platform()==='linux', isWaylandSession() and process.env.WAYLAND_DISPLAY is truthy. It executes wl-paste --no-newline --type text with UTF-8, 50 MiB maxBuffer and 5000 ms timeout. A successful command returns its text or null for empty and never falls through. A command exception falls back to addon getText. Missing addon returns null; getText errors are caught and an empty result becomes null. This helper has no SSH guard of its own (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:35-71).

Tests read cover fallback require roots, absent addon, Wayland precedence, authoritative empty Wayland data and native read failure. No operating-system clipboard was accessed by this audit.
entries.interfaces: ClipboardModule {getText, setText, hasImage, getImageBinary}; loadClipboardNative(requires?)→ClipboardModule|null; readClipboardText()→Promise<string|null>. Environment gates are evaluated at module initialization for addon availability; text backend selection is evaluated per call.
entries.dependency_text: MISC-006 owns isWaylandSession and image backend selection. TUI owns paste-key routing and when remote clipboard reads are permitted.
entries.rust: Native read_clipboard_text constructs arboard::Clipboard and calls get_text, returning None on either failure. It compiles to None without the clipboard feature or on Android. The feature is enabled by default, and its dependency is excluded for Android (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/run.rs:395-407; rust:crates/ice-cli/Cargo.toml:56-60; rust:crates/ice-cli/Cargo.toml:95-98). There is no explicit source-level Wayland command precedence or two-root addon fallback in that helper. The library's own platform internals were not inspected and are not assumed incapable of clipboard support.
entries.port: Keep arboard and the native feature gate. Add explicit text-backend precedence and empty-versus-failed handling where a platform needs TS-compatible Wayland fallback; keep policy in the caller and avoid stale-backend fallback after a successful empty read. Node module resolution requires no native emulation.
entries.priority_reason: Backend precedence can paste stale text, while an optional clipboard dependency must remain safe in headless and Android builds.

entries.title: Ordered clipboard writes and bounded remote OSC 52 fallback
entries.what: Clipboard copy selects platform backends in a defined order and supplements remote sessions with a bounded OSC 52 write. Success means at least one backend accepted the copy; the fallback sequence must not report success merely because a child was spawned.
entries.mechanism:
TS tries a direct clipboard write before terminal escape output. Remote sessions can receive OSC 52 after a successful native write, while local success returns without issuing duplicate terminal clipboard writes.

copyToClipboard first calls addon.setText on platforms other than linux and catches failure. A successful local write returns. Remote means any truthy SSH_CONNECTION, SSH_CLIENT or MOSH_CONNECTION. If not yet copied, darwin executes pbcopy and win32 clip; otherwise it tries termux-clipboard-set when TERMUX_VERSION is truthy, then Wayland/X11. These synchronous command writes use input:text,5000 ms timeout and ignored stdout/stderr. X11 tries xclip -selection clipboard then xsel --clipboard --input (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:12-24; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:73-125).

Wayland is selected only with isWaylandSession and a truthy WAYLAND_DISPLAY. It first execs 'which wl-copy' without the 5000 ms options, then spawns wl-copy with piped stdin and ignored output. It ignores stdin EPIPE, writes/ends text, and resolves success only on close code 0; error/null/nonzero counts failure. This asynchronous branch has no timeout. With DISPLAY present, failure falls back to X11; without Wayland selection, DISPLAY alone uses X11. Outer failures fall through (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:126-165).

When remote or still uncopied, emitOsc52 base64-encodes UTF-8 and refuses encoded length>100000. Otherwise it writes ESC]52;c;<base64>BEL to process.stdout and returns true without waiting for an acknowledgment or drain. copied becomes priorCopied||osc52Copied. If all attempts fail, throw 'Failed to copy to clipboard'. An oversized remote OSC payload does not turn a prior native success into failure. Tests specify local direct/shell success skipping OSC, remote ordering, fallback and size refusal; no copy was executed (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:26-32; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:167-174; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/clipboard.test.ts:151-210).
entries.interfaces: copyToClipboard(text):Promise<void>; OSC 52 selection 'c', BEL terminator, encoded ceiling 100000. External programs: pbcopy, clip, termux-clipboard-set, which, wl-copy, xclip, xsel. No clipboard text is persisted by this helper.
entries.dependency_text: The TUI caller owns /copy, selection content and user-facing feedback. This entry owns backend order, transport limits and success/failure semantics.
entries.rust: Native copy_to_clipboard only constructs arboard and returns set_text(...).is_ok(), otherwise false; disabled/Android builds always return false (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/run.rs:379-393). The inspected crates search found no OSC52, wl-copy, pbcopy, xclip or Termux command fallback. This is source evidence for the local product helper, not a claim about every library's internal platform implementation.
entries.port: Keep the native API but add a clipboard service with ordered platform backends and bounded OSC 52 fallback when remote copying is required. Preserve the distinction between empty/read failure and copy acknowledgment. Give spawned fallback commands an owned timeout/cancellation policy; do not copy TS's unbounded wl-copy wait merely for incidental parity.
entries.priority_reason: Remote and Wayland users can lose a working copy path when only the native clipboard backend is available.

entries.title: Clipboard image backend order, MIME preference and WSL transfer
entries.what: Clipboard images follow a different fallback sequence from clipboard text. TS supports Wayland/X11 negotiation and a WSL PowerShell bridge, while Rust already supplies native bitmap capture and copied-file handling.
entries.mechanism:
TS chooses an image backend from the current platform and environment, then converts unsupported returned formats to PNG. Its image MIME preference and WSL fallback are explicit, so a generic clipboard call alone does not establish the same behavior.

readClipboardImage({env?, platform?}) defaults to process.env/process.platform and returns null immediately for truthy TERMUX_VERSION. isWaylandSession is truthy WAYLAND_DISPLAY or XDG_SESSION_TYPE exactly 'wayland'. WSL means truthy WSL_DISTRO_NAME/WSLENV or /proc/version matching microsoft|wsl case-insensitively; read failure means false. On linux, Wayland or WSL tries wl-paste then xclip. If still empty and WSL, try PowerShell. If still empty and not Wayland, try native addon then xclip. Nonlinux tries the native addon. Native hasImage/getImageBinary calls are not wrapped in a catch here, so their exceptions can reject; absent/false/empty returns null (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard-image.ts:143-154; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard-image.ts:240-299).

runCommand uses spawnSync, default 3000 ms and 50 MiB maxBuffer, returning ok:false on spawn error or nonzero status. Listing has 1000 ms. wl-paste --list-types chooses preferred normalized base MIME in order PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, then the first image/*; it requests the original selected string with --type and --no-newline, returns base MIME and nonempty bytes. xclip first requests TARGETS, then tries preferred (if any) followed by the four supported MIME types without deduplicating, accepting the first nonempty successful output. The env option used for backend selection is not forwarded to these calls; the child inherits process environment unless a runCommand caller explicitly supplies env (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard-image.ts:15-65; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard-image.ts:89-141; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard-image.ts:213-238).

The WSL bridge creates a UUID PNG path under tmpdir, maps it with wslpath -w within 1000 ms, doubles apostrophes in the resulting Windows path, and embeds that literal in a PowerShell script loading Forms/Drawing and saving GetImage to PNG. powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command has 5000 ms. Only output trimmed exactly 'ok' permits reading the nonempty temporary file. Any bridge exception returns null, and unlink is attempted in finally. There is no custom environment variable transport (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard-image.ts:161-211).

Supported returned MIME bases are PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF; unknown image formats such as BMP are decoded by Photon and re-encoded PNG, returning null if unavailable/failing. This clipboard-local converter frees its image but does not call the EXIF-orientation helper. extensionForImageMimeType returns png/jpg/webp/gif after parameter removal, trim and lowercase; image/jpg is not one of its accepted cases. Read tests assert Wayland/native selection, xclip fallback, escaped WSL path transport and BMP conversion without executing clipboard operations.
entries.interfaces: ClipboardImage={bytes:Uint8Array, mimeType:string}; readClipboardImage({env?, platform?})→Promise<ClipboardImage|null>; isWaylandSession(env?)→boolean; extensionForImageMimeType(mime)→string|null. Temporary file: <tmpdir>/ice-wsl-clip-<uuid>.png.
entries.dependency_text: TOOLS-023 owns shared image codec/resize helpers; this entry owns clipboard acquisition and its separate converter. Root's native run.rs443–725 source credit supplies copied-file parsing/previews; TUI owns input routing and model-image settings.
entries.rust: Native bitmap capture is enabled with clipboard outside Android, uses arboard, treats get_image failure as None, checks nonzero width/height≤16384, encodes RGBA8 PNG and returns base64. Other construction/conversion failures become Err strings (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/run.rs:409-441). It also has actual macOS osascript alias-list and Windows CF_HDROP copied-file readers, all-or-nothing quoted/escaped path image parsing, and width 60 preview conversion; these are preserved native capabilities, credited from root's complete helper read (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/run.rs:443-725). No explicit WSL PowerShell or negotiated wl-paste/xclip sequence appears in this helper. Helpers themselves have no SSH/blockImages gate; root independently established the main caller's SSH check applies only to text fallback, not bitmap/file reads.
entries.port: Keep native bitmap limits and copied-file support. Add explicit WSL/Wayland image fallback if required, retain time/buffer bounds and guaranteed temporary-file cleanup, and choose whether native addon exceptions should be surfaced or treated as fallback. Keep clipboard acquisition distinct from subsequent image normalization and display-only show_images. Do not infer blockImages policy from preview visibility.
entries.priority_reason: Clipboard image acquisition varies materially across Wayland, WSL and remote sessions even though both products have real image support.

entries.title: Cancellation linking, waiter races and abortable timer lifetime
entries.what: Link an operation to a caller's cancellation signal and stop waiting promptly without abandoning the underlying promise's rejection. Timer and listener ownership are part of the contract, while Rust uses cancellation tokens and dropped futures instead of JavaScript promises.
entries.mechanism:
A cancelled caller can stop waiting even when the operation itself is still settling. The helper preserves the caller's cancellation reason and removes the listener once the race has a winner.

linkAbortSignal(controller, signal?) immediately aborts the controller with signal.reason if the supplied signal is already aborted; otherwise it conditionally installs a once-only listener. Every call returns a closure that conditionally removes that listener, including absent or already-aborted signals. operationSignal returns the supplied signal by identity or a fresh AbortController signal; it creates no timeout or implicit cancellation scope. raceWithAbortSignal returns the original promise unchanged when there is no signal. With a pre-aborted signal it attaches a rejection observer to the operation before returning a rejection, so later operation failure is consumed. With a live signal it creates one settled flag, installs a once-only listener, registers operation fulfillment/rejection, and rechecks aborted after registration to close the setup window. Whichever callback wins removes the listener; later callbacks cannot change the result. The abort result is signal.reason unless undefined, in which case it uses an ordinary Error('The operation was aborted') whose name is set to AbortError. Racing does not abort or kill the underlying operation (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/abort.ts:1-57).

The separate sleep(ms, signal) rejects with ordinary Error('Aborted') for both pre-abort and later abort, discarding a caller-specific reason. Its abort handler clears the timeout. Unlike raceWithAbortSignal, it does not use once and does not remove the listener on successful timer completion, so a long-lived signal can retain completed timer closures; this is source behavior to correct rather than deliberately recreate. There is no helper-level retry (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/sleep.ts:1-19). No direct dedicated test suite for these two coding-agent utilities was found by the recorded import/function search; their session, auth and subagent consumers have independently assigned source-only tests.
entries.interfaces: linkAbortSignal(controller:AbortController, signal?:AbortSignal):()=>void; operationSignal(signal?:AbortSignal):AbortSignal; raceWithAbortSignal<T>(operation:Promise<T>, signal:AbortSignal|undefined):Promise<T>; sleep(ms:number, signal?:AbortSignal):Promise<void>. Cancellation can carry any JS reason; abort.ts uses an ordinary Error named AbortError only when signal.reason is undefined.
entries.dependency_text: AI-001/002, SESSION-018, AUTH-015 and SUB-008 own the actual retry, refresh, auth and approval integration. This entry specifies shared helper ownership and does not add their execution behavior or LOC again.
entries.rust: Native compaction waits with tokio::select! over sleep and signal.cancelled(), normalizing cancellation to StopReason::Aborted and clearing error_message. ChildTool uses biased select so an already-ready cancellation branch wins before the wrapped child execution; it passes signal.child_token() to the tool and maps cancellation to a typed tool error string. These are genuine cancellation implementations rather than a missing AbortController class (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/compaction/compaction.rs:451-495; rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness/child.rs:34-51). Rust futures/tokens do not reproduce JS promise identity or arbitrary signal.reason object identity at these boundaries.
entries.port: Keep Rust cancellation-token/future ownership and the subsystem-specific settlement rules. Where a public adapter exposes cancellation reasons, map them explicitly instead of requiring JS object identity. Ensure any new waiter unregisters on both success and cancellation and continues to observe independently spawned task failure. Do not copy sleep's completed-listener retention. No standalone runtime subsystem is missing, so incremental implementation LOC is zero here.
entries.priority_reason: Cancellation cleanup must be explicit, but the native execution paths already implement cancellation; duplicate helper implementation would overcount the port.

entries.title: Filesystem watcher error callbacks versus native modification-time polling
entries.what: Shared watcher helpers define setup failure, error notification and stop ownership. The native implementation polls modification times rather than subscribing to operating-system watch events, which changes detection and error semantics.
entries.mechanism:
The TS helper reports watcher errors to its caller and leaves retry scheduling to that caller. Native Rust uses a polling task with an owned stop flag, so it observes snapshot changes rather than the exact same event stream.

FS_WATCH_RETRY_DELAY_MS=5000 is a constant only. closeWatcher accepts null/undefined and swallows close errors. watchWithErrorHandler calls fs.watch(path, listener), attaches watcher.on('error', onError), and returns it; a synchronous failure invokes onError and returns null. It does not close the watcher, debounce, retry, impose a timer, normalize filenames or catch later listener/onError exceptions. A synchronous onError exception in the catch propagates. Footer/theme callers own rearming and teardown (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/fs-watch.ts:3-30).

Native watch_paths starts a Tokio task, captures the initial path→optional mtime map, sleeps the requested interval before each comparison and calls on_change once when the map differs. Missing paths and metadata/modified errors all map to None; they do not enter the 5000 ms retry path. Only panic caught during a later snapshot causes that retry sleep; the initial snapshot and callback are outside that catch. watch_path defaults 1000 ms. A callback panic ends the task. request_stop and Drop set the atomic flag; close sets it and aborts the stored join handle without awaiting completion. The comments saying Drop does not stop and close waits are contradicted by the body (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/fs_watch.rs:18-112).

The two inline native tests assert eventual mtime-change callback and a close call; they were read, not executed, and do not prove byte-content detection when mtime is unchanged, error callbacks or joined shutdown. No direct TS fs-watch test was found; footer/theme consumer suites are credited to TUI.

entries.title: Shared YAML frontmatter fences, scalar values and parse errors
entries.what: Prompt, skill and subagent loaders share a frontmatter parser whose fence and whitespace rules affect both metadata and executable prompt text. Parsed YAML is not restricted to an object by the TS helper's runtime implementation.
entries.mechanism:
TS normalizes line endings before locating a leading frontmatter block. It trims the body only when a closing fence was found, and malformed YAML propagates an error even when the caller only asked to strip metadata.

Normalize CRLF then bare CR to LF. The opener check is startsWith('---'), not a whole-line delimiter check. Find the first '\n---' starting at index 3; absent opener/closer yields frontmatter:{} and the entire normalized, untrimmed body. With a closer, yamlString is slice(4, endIndex) and body is slice(endIndex+4).trim(), so characters following the three closing hyphens belong to body. Empty/falsy yamlString returns {}; otherwise yaml.parse is called and only null/undefined is converted to {}. The generic Record type is a cast: scalar/array values are returned as parsed. stripFrontmatter calls this parser and can therefore throw YAML errors (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/frontmatter.ts:8-39).

The direct suite specifies quoted keys/values, CRLF, invalid-YAML location text, literal block scalars ending in a newline, missing/unterminated fences, comment-only {} and untrimmed no-frontmatter bodies. These are inspected assertions only (ice:packages/coding-agent/test/frontmatter.test.ts:4-60).

Native normalizes the same newlines and largely copies the delimiter/slice contract using safe UTF-8 get ranges. parse_yaml returns an empty object for whitespace-only input but otherwise directly returns yaml_serde::from_str's Value. On a parse error it retries only after quoting unindented noncomment top-level scalar values containing ': ' unless they begin a quote/collection/block-scalar marker; it preserves the original error if that repair fails. This deliberate legacy repair is absent in TS (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/frontmatter.rs:22-89).
entries.interfaces: parseFrontmatter<T>(content)→{frontmatter:T, body:string}; stripFrontmatter(content)→string. External parsing library: yaml in TS, yaml_serde in Rust. No disk I/O or trust check occurs here; callers own metadata validation.
entries.dependency_text: Prompt-template, skill and subagent entries retain their schema/trust/resource ownership. This entry owns only shared extraction, YAML value normalization and error behavior.
entries.rust: Native has a real shared YAML parser, nested mappings, sequences and block scalars, with inline tests covering these. It accepts legacy unquoted top-level ': ' scalar text that TS rejects. It lacks the TS post-parse nullish→{} normalization, and its block-scalar inline assertion expects 'First line\nSecond line' while the TS helper test expects a terminal newline for the corresponding literal style (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/frontmatter.rs:44-61; rust:crates/ice-harness/src/frontmatter.rs:151-170). These source/test contract differences require reconciliation; no parser was executed. Native safe byte-range slicing also differs from TS UTF-16 slice for malformed opener text containing non-ASCII characters, so whole-line fence normalization should be an explicit policy.
entries.port: Preserve full native YAML support and decide whether legacy scalar repair remains an intentional compatibility feature. Add explicit nullish-to-object normalization where TS consumers rely on it, preserve body trimming/newline behavior and carry parse errors to the same diagnostic boundary. Compare scalar/array/null/comment-only values and block scalar chomping with meaningful future tests; do not impose object validation inside this helper unless every caller contract is updated.
entries.priority_reason: Subtle YAML and whitespace differences can change prompt contents or accepted definitions despite broadly equivalent loader functionality.

entries.title: Optional fd and rg discovery, download selection and extraction policy
entries.what: TypeScript can discover or provision fd and rg when its external search backends require them. Rust's existing search implementations run in process, so absence of this downloader is not itself a search capability gap.
entries.mechanism:
The helper prefers a previously installed local executable and then a discovered system command. When neither exists, online non-Android TypeScript sessions may download a platform release and install it in the application bin directory.

TOOLS_DIR is captured from getBinDir at module initialization. Definitions are fd from sharkdp/fd with system names fd then fdfind, and rg from BurntSushi/ripgrep with system name rg. getToolPath first accepts an existing local binary path without checking file kind or executability. It next uses a positive per-tool system-name cache; probes run '<name> --version' synchronously with piped output and no timeout, and accept any result without a spawn error, even a nonzero status. Failed probes are not cached. Existing local/system results are returned before checking offline or platform restrictions (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tools-manager.ts:1-110).

ensureTool(tool, silent=false) recognizes ICE_OFFLINE values 1/true/yes case-insensitively without trimming. Missing tools in that mode produce optional warnings and undefined. Android produces package-manager guidance and undefined. Otherwise it optionally logs, attempts download, returns the installed path, and catches failures into warning/undefined. No user confirmation is implemented by this helper. Release metadata uses the GitHub latest-release API, User-Agent '<APP_NAME>-coding-agent', a 10-second timeout and unvalidated tag_name with the first 'v' removed. Platform archive templates support Darwin, Linux and Windows with arm64 or otherwise x64; unsupported platforms fail only after metadata lookup. fd on Darwin x64 is pinned to 10.3.0 after the latest-version request. Archive download has a 120-second fetch timeout but no checksum, signature or explicit byte limit (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tools-manager.ts:112-177; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tools-manager.ts:333-377).

Downloads use a shared archive filename in TOOLS_DIR and a unique extraction directory. tar handles tar.gz; Windows zip extraction prefers the system tar executable and falls back to PowerShell Expand-Archive with escaped literal paths; other zip platforms try unzip then tar. Extraction subprocesses have no deadline. The executable lookup first accepts expected archive-subdirectory and root paths when they merely exist, then traverses subdirectories to find a regular file with the expected name. It renames into the final bin path, applies 0755 on Unix, and removes archive/extraction paths in finally. A download or temporary-directory failure before the try/finally can leave an archive, and concurrent same-tool downloads share archive/destination paths without single-flight protection. The source performs no archive-containment check of its own. These limitations are not requirements to weaken the native installer (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tools-manager.ts:178-330).

The only direct test-directory import match was a UI test mocking ensureTool; no dedicated downloader behavior suite was found by the recorded function/import search. Existing tools tests cover the search consumers, not real release downloads. Nothing was executed or downloaded in this audit.
entries.interfaces: getToolPath('fd'|'rg')→string|null; ensureTool('fd'|'rg', silent=false)→Promise<string|undefined>; application bin directory, external fd/fdfind/rg commands, GitHub release metadata/assets, ICE_OFFLINE, SystemRoot/WINDIR on Windows.

entries.title: Coding-agent shell selection, environment and shutdown wrapper
entries.what: The coding-agent wrapper selects a usable shell, exposes its application bin directory to child commands, sanitizes display text and tracks detached process cleanup. Most native process machinery already exists; the remaining application environment integration must be distinguished from generic shell execution.
entries.mechanism:
Commands use an explicit executable and argument transport selected for the platform. The application wrapper also prepares PATH and maintains a process-wide set of detached children for shutdown.

A truthy custom shell path wins if it merely exists, otherwise throws 'Custom shell path not found'. A Windows path matching a drive-qualified Windows/System32 or Sysnative bash.exe, case-insensitively after slash normalization, uses ['-s'] with commandTransport='stdin'; other shells use ['-c']. Windows probes ProgramFiles/Git/bin/bash.exe, then ProgramFiles(x86)/Git/bin/bash.exe, then where bash.exe with a 5000 ms timeout/windowsHide. Only the first returned line is tested for existence; a bad first result does not try the later lines. Missing Windows bash throws multiline installation/settings guidance. Unix prefers /bin/bash, then a successful which bash invocation with 5000 ms timeout and its first nonempty trimmed line without a further filesystem check, then sh. All existence checks concern existence, not executable permission or regular-file kind (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/shell.ts:15-120).

getShellEnv recomputes getBinDir, chooses the first enumerable ambient key whose lowercase spelling is 'path', otherwise PATH, and splits its value on the platform path delimiter. Exact string membership of binDir suppresses insertion; otherwise binDir is prepended while preserving the original PATH string. The result is a shallow copy of process.env with only that chosen key overwritten. It does not canonicalize paths, compare case-insensitively, remove duplicate alternative PATH keys or mutate process.env. TOOLS-002 then clears inherited session metadata and injects the current opted-in session environment before invoking the spawn hook (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/shell.ts:122-134; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts:201-255).

sanitizeBinaryOutput iterates JS code points, retains tab/LF/CR, removes code points <=0x1f and U+FFF9–FFFB, then joins. Despite its comment, Array.from does not itself remove lone surrogate code units, and the predicate does not reject them; it also does not remove all Unicode Format characters or DEL. Dropping ESC alone leaves the printable suffix of an ANSI sequence. These exact limitations must not be described as comprehensive terminal sanitization (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/shell.ts:136-174).

Detached PID tracking uses Set add/delete, and shutdown iterates killProcessTree then clears the set. Unix group liveness sends signal 0 to -pgid, treating EPERM as alive. terminateProcessGroup defaults to 3000 ms, sends SIGTERM, polls every 100 ms and stops as soon as the group disappears; only a continuously existing group is eventually SIGKILLed. Its timer is unref'd. killProcessTree spawns detached hidden taskkill /F /T /PID on Windows with ignored stdio and no wait/unref, or SIGKILLs the Unix group with PID fallback; exceptions are swallowed. TOOLS-008 and SESSION-023/025 own the actual background registry and disposal callers, rather than a second registry here (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/shell.ts:176-269). The recorded direct-test symbol search found no additional dedicated shell-wrapper suite; generic shell and background-tool tests remain with their owners.
entries.interfaces: ShellConfig {shell, args, commandTransport?}; getShellConfig(customShellPath?); getShellEnv(); sanitizeBinaryOutput(string); trackDetachedChildPid/untrackDetachedChildPid/killTrackedDetachedChildren; isProcessGroupAlive; terminateProcessGroup(graceMs=3000); killProcessTree. Ambient ProgramFiles, ProgramFiles(x86) and the first case-insensitive PATH key affect resolution.
entries.dependency_text: AGENT-048–054 own generic shell configuration/environment/capture/kill/cleanup algorithms. TOOLS-002 owns current-session environment and spawn hooks; TOOLS-008/010 own background cleanup/output. MISC-010 explains why native Find/Grep need no downloaded executables. Only application PATH integration and any agreed coding-wrapper compatibility correction are counted here.
entries.rust: Native os_env has explicit shell selection, Windows Git Bash/PATH probing, legacy WSL stdin transport and Unix /bin/bash/which/sh fallbacks. Its Unix which output is treated as one trimmed path and checked for existence, differing from the TS coding wrapper's first-line trust. Native child execution clears inherited environment, rebuilds a filtered host environment, then applies base and extra overrides; no getBinDir-style application PATH prepend occurs in that reviewed spawn path. Host-private session/subagent environment filtering is an existing native protection, not a gap (rust:crates/ice-tools/src/os_env.rs:175-227; rust:crates/ice-tools/src/os_env.rs:295-354; rust:crates/ice-tools/src/os_env.rs:840-867). Those stronger/different mechanics should not be replaced merely to copy JS limitations.
entries.port: Define the application-owned child PATH once at the native CLI/tool integration boundary and preserve private-environment filtering and explicit override order. Add application bin exposure only for tools that actually use it, without making native Find/Grep depend on fd or rg. Resolve the first-line shell discovery difference deliberately. Reuse existing process-group and output machinery under its owners; do not port the misleading lone-surrogate claim or degrade full-sequence ANSI sanitation. Keep mode shutdown connected to the one tracked background owner.
entries.priority_reason: Native shell execution is substantial already; exact application PATH and wrapper boundaries prevent both small compatibility failures and duplicated port estimates.

entries.title: Browser and default-handler process ownership
entries.what: Open a URL or file through the platform's default handler without invoking a command shell, while keeping launcher output and lifetime separate from the agent's terminal or protocol stream.
entries.mechanism:
The helper starts the platform launcher and immediately returns. It treats opening as best effort, because the caller also displays the destination.

Darwin runs open with the target as one argument; Windows runs rundll32 with arguments ['url.dll,FileProtocolHandler', target]; every other TS platform runs xdg-open with one target argument. It never constructs a shell command and does not use cmd /c start. There is no URL-scheme allowlist or target normalization in this generic helper. spawn uses stdio:'ignore' and detached:true, installs an error listener that ignores asynchronous spawn errors, then unrefs the child. It neither waits for the launcher exit status nor confirms that a browser displayed the target. A synchronous exceptional call is not surrounded by a local try/catch (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/open-browser.ts:10-23).

The matching regression test discovered in the test tree mocks this helper to inspect the OAuth prompt flow; it is not evidence that a real platform browser launched. The native module's inline tests inspect platform selection and argument structure without opening a browser. All evidence is source-only.
entries.interfaces: openBrowser(target:string)→void. Native open_browser/open_file return Result<(), String>; target is a distinct process argument in both designs. Platform commands: open, rundll32 url.dll, FileProtocolHandler, xdg-open.
entries.dependency_text: Provider login and TUI presentation own when and whether a destination is offered/opened; OBS-014 owns dashboard URL/token policy. This helper owns only native launcher process/stdio behavior, not those destinations' trust or protocol semantics.
entries.rust: The native helper uses the same argument-vector commands for macOS, Windows and supported Linux/BSD platforms, and returns an unsupported-platform error elsewhere. It returns success when spawn succeeds, without waiting for launcher completion. Its Command does not configure null stdio or detachment/unref semantics, so the child inherits the current standard streams. It preserves spawn errors in Result rather than ignoring them (rust:crates/ice-tools/src/utils/open_browser.rs:17-85; rust:crates/ice-tools/src/utils/open_browser.rs:88-168). Shell avoidance is already present; absence of a whole browser helper is an incorrect gap claim.
entries.port: Keep the native argument-vector launch and useful Result error reporting. Configure launcher stdin/stdout/stderr and process ownership explicitly so opening a page cannot read from or write into an agent protocol stream. Preserve platform-specific child reaping/detachment appropriate to Rust rather than translating JS unref literally. Let callers continue showing a manual target when automatic launch fails.
entries.priority_reason: The key launch mechanism exists; isolating inherited streams and clarifying error ownership are bounded integration corrections.

entries.title: Changelog parsing, version filtering and release-pinned links
entries.what: Parse release entries and make links from displayed historical release notes resolve against the matching repository tag, while preserving the native bundled changelog and first-run baseline policy.
entries.mechanism:
The helper extracts versioned sections from a local changelog and filters them against a prior version. Link normalization separately pins relative and selected floating GitHub links to the displayed release.

parseChangelog returns [] when the path is absent; read/parse exceptions warn to console.error and return []. Only lines starting exactly '## ' begin a boundary. At each boundary it saves the preceding recognized entry, then matches three decimal components with optional square brackets using the source regex; this is a prefix match, not strict semver validation. A recognized entry retains its heading in content. An unrecognized '## ' section clears the current entry, so its body is not appended to the prior release. Entries remain in file order, content is trimmed, and no deduplication/sort occurs. compareVersions returns the arithmetic component difference, despite the comment's -1/0/1 shorthand. getNewEntries splits the supplied baseline on '.', applies Number and falls back to zero for falsy components, then keeps entries whose comparison is >0 in original order (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/changelog.ts:107-193).

normalizeChangelogLinks handles the source inline Markdown-link/image regex only; reference-style links, raw HTML and general Markdown parsing are not implemented. It prefixes a version with lowercase v unless it already starts with v. Exact badlogic or earendil-works ice-mono/pi-mono GitHub repository prefixes become Zykairotis/ice; unrelated repositories remain unchanged. For that canonical repository, blob/tree URLs under main or master are pinned to the release tag. Fragment-only, protocol-relative and any explicit-scheme targets are otherwise preserved (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/changelog.ts:11-105).

For a relative target, split hash then query, normalize backslashes, resolve from packages/coding-agent or repository root when slash-prefixed, and reject normalized '.'/'..'/leading '../' by retaining the original target. A trailing slash or basename without a dot selects tree; otherwise blob. encodeURI applies to the repository path, while query and fragment retain their original spelling. This is a link-rewrite heuristic, not filesystem existence checking or URL access. Tests cover relative paths, tag pinning and exact historical repository aliases; no network fetch or rendered navigation was executed (ice:packages/coding-agent/test/changelog.test.ts:1-50).
entries.interfaces: ChangelogEntry {major, minor, patch, content}; parseChangelog(path), compareVersions, getNewEntries(entries, lastVersion), normalizeChangelogLinks(markdown, version). Native public configuration additionally includes ICERS_CHANGELOG_URL and allow_network; those are retained native facilities, not TS helper inputs.

entries.title: Application ANSI stripping and exact control-sequence compatibility
entries.what: Remove selected terminal control sequences from application text while preserving ordinary text and the helper's exact input contract. Reuse the native terminal stripping implementation, with the differences between its scanner and the TS compatibility regex made explicit.
entries.mechanism:
The application helper strips recognized escape sequences from a string and returns plain text. It has an exact runtime type check and a fast path, while the native implementation accepts only valid Rust strings and uses a scanner.

stripAnsi rejects every non-string JS value, including a boxed String, with TypeError whose message is Expected a `string`, got `<typeof value>`. When neither ESC U+001B nor C1 CSI U+009B is present, it returns the original string directly. Otherwise it calls String.replace with one cached global regex; replace resets the regex cursor, so repeated calls do not inherit a prior lastIndex. The module contains the upstream MIT notice, which remains relevant if code is copied (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/ansi.ts:1-27; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/ansi.ts:44-60).

The OSC alternative recognizes ESC ] followed by the shortest sequence through BEL, ESC backslash, or C1 ST U+009C. The second alternative starts with ESC or C1 CSI and applies the source's finite intermediate/parameter/final-character grammar: optional bracket/parenthesis/#/semicolon/question characters, optional one-to-four-digit parameters with semicolon or colon separators, then the listed final-character classes. It is a compatibility regex rather than a complete ECMA control parser. Unknown, malformed or unterminated sequences can remain wholly or partially in the output; APC/DCS/PM and raw C1 OSC are not generally consumed as complete strings by this grammar. The helper does not HTML-escape content, remove every control character, or calculate terminal width (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/ansi.ts:29-42).

The source suite compares generated escape inputs with an inline reference containing the same regex, checks non-string errors, RIS and selected one-byte escapes, and a combined SGR/OSC8 example. That establishes intended regex compatibility, not independent proof of complete protocol coverage. No tests were executed, and the native inline tests cover simple SGR stripping and width rather than the TS C1/terminator matrix (ice:packages/coding-agent/test/ansi-utils.test.ts:4-109; rust:crates/ice-tui/src/ansi.rs:194-220).
entries.interfaces: stripAnsi(value:string)→string; invalid JS runtime types throw TypeError. Recognized introducers include ESC and C1 CSI; OSC terminators include BEL, ESC backslash and C1 ST. The native equivalent is ice_tui::ansi::strip_ansi(&str)→String.

MISC-011 owns the different shell binary-output sanitizer. This entry records the application helper compatibility boundary and adds no duplicate parser LOC.
entries.rust: Native strip_ansi scans characters and enters escape handling only on ESC, so raw C1 CSI is retained. It consumes ordinary CSI through a final byte, handles the private cursor marker, and strips ESC OSC/APC/DCS/PM through BEL or ESC backslash. It does not recognize C1 ST in those strings, and an unterminated string consumes the rest of the input. Character-set designation and generic two-character escape branches are also present. These are real existing controls, some broader and some narrower than the TS regex; they must not be called exact parity or a missing stripping engine (rust:crates/ice-tui/src/ansi.rs:21-87). Rust's &str type removes the JS dynamic-type and lone-surrogate cases from the native function's input domain.

If C1 handling is required, correct it in the one shared terminal parser under TUI-201 and exercise the actual supported terminators there. Preserve error translation at any JS-facing adapter without adding dynamic-type checks to ordinary Rust callers. Do not duplicate terminal-parser LOC or replace the scanner with a regex merely to recreate malformed-sequence behavior.

entries.title: Single-shot text prompts, final-message output and cleanup
entries.what: Run initial and additional prompts sequentially, print the final session message's text, and dispose the runtime once. Native text mode already works, but its retained-message state can print an earlier answer after the final prompt fails.
entries.mechanism:
Text mode drives the current runtime session and emits only its final assistant text. It also owns the mode's subscriptions and runtime shutdown, including a bounded set of process signal handlers.

runPrintMode defaults messages to [], keeps a mutable session reference and registers SIGTERM everywhere plus SIGHUP outside Windows. A signal first kills tracked detached children, then starts disposeRuntime and exits from finally with 143 or 129. disposeRuntime sets its once flag before unsubscribing and awaiting runtimeHost.dispose; a throwing unsubscribe/dispose cannot be retried through that flag. This module adds no local SIGINT handler. Ordinary finally removes the registered handlers, awaits disposal, then flushes raw stdout; an unexpected disposal rejection can override an intended return and skip the later flush. These exceptional cleanup limitations should be strengthened in a port, not called guaranteed cleanup (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/print-mode.ts:33-68; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/print-mode.ts:158-168).

The host's rebind callback refreshes the mutable session and binds extensions in print or json mode with waitForIdle/newSession/fork/navigateTree/switchSession/reload actions. It forwards navigate summary/custom-instruction/replace/label options and returns only cancelled from fork/navigation. Extension errors go to stderr. A truthy initialMessage is prompted first with initialImages; empty initial text is skipped and does not independently submit its images. Each messages item is then prompted sequentially on the current mutable session without those initial images. Text mode inspects exactly state.messages[last], not the last assistant anywhere in history and not a cached per-run outcome. entries.title: Single-shot JSON event framing, backpressure and watch lifetime
entries.what: Emit a session header followed by a delta-only JSONL event stream, and stop every event producer when the mode ends. Native JSON mode has a real live stream, but its framing, completion barrier and retained watch differ materially.
entries.mechanism:
TypeScript JSON mode emits the initial session header before extension binding, then writes each subscribed session event as one JSON line. It applies output backpressure through a separate awaited agent subscriber and disposes both subscriptions at completion.

The header comes from sessionManager.getHeader and is emitted only when present. Rebinding later updates the session subscription but does not emit another header in this function. toJsonEvent preserves non-message_update events; message_update drops the cumulative message snapshot and removes assistantMessageEvent.partial, retaining the remaining event fields. This keeps incremental stream size from multiplying cumulative snapshots; message_end remains authoritative. The separate agent subscriber awaits waitForRawStdoutBackpressure after the session-event writer, and final cleanup awaits flushRawStdout after runtime disposal (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/print-mode.ts:108-138; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/print-mode.ts:162-168; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/json-event.ts:1-41).

The text-only final assistant stopReason check does not run in JSON mode. A resolved prompt whose resulting assistant is error/aborted can therefore still return 0 here; a thrown prompt/runtime error returns 1 with stderr text. This helper does not add a terminal {'type':'result'} record. Queue and compaction events come from the session's shared event contract, not new JSON-only state (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/print-mode.ts:139-161; ice:packages/coding-agent/docs/json.md:9-26; ice:packages/coding-agent/docs/json.md:62-85).

The same mode signal/rebinding/cleanup limitations described in MISC-015 apply. Existing tests were read as source only; no stream, subprocess, pipe or integration test was run.
entries.interfaces: --mode json single-shot output: optional initial SessionHeader, then JsonAgentSessionEvent JSONL, with delta-only message_update and authoritative message_end. No command-input protocol or TS terminal result record is implied. Shared stopReason serialization is owned by RPC-017.
entries.dependency_text: RPC-017 owns JsonAgentSessionEvent mapping, raw stream guard and the live ToolUse serde mismatch; this entry owns single-shot framing/lifetime and avoids duplicating wire DTO LOC. SESSION owns lifecycle, retry/queue/compaction events. CLI-019 owns outer startup/output cleanup.
entries.rust:
Native json installs a harness watch that immediately printlns each event and pushes a clone into an Arc<Mutex<Vec<HarnessEvent>>>. The collection is never read in this function. std::mem::forget(watch) deliberately retains the callback and its collection for the remaining event-bus lifetime; memory therefore grows with observed harness events, and reusing the harness for another json invocation retains earlier output listeners. Single-shot process exit may bound duration, but does not make the collection bounded (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/modes.rs:156-170). A second spawned task streams native AgentEvents; broadcast lag is silently skipped. Terminal notices use an unbounded unit channel, and each prompt waits at most 250 ms for an uncorrelated terminal notice rather than a per-run flush barrier. The task is aborted at the end (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/modes.rs:172-235).

Native output ends with {type:'result', outcome:'completed'|'aborted'|'failed'|'suspended'|'idle', finalText:string|null}, omits the TS initial header, and maps Failed/Aborted to exit 1 while Suspended returns 0 through outcome_exit_code. Direct println bypasses the bounded single-writer service already implemented by native RPC. Thus native streaming is present, but its wire and cleanup semantics are not equivalent (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/modes.rs:43-47; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/modes.rs:237-266; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/modes.rs:314-349).
entries.port: Reuse the existing bounded native writer and event flush mechanism for JSON single-shot mode. Retain the watch handle and drop it on every exit; remove the unused collection, or bound it only if a documented summary needs it. Correlate terminal completion to the actual run and drain its events before returning instead of relying on a 250 ms unit-notice race. Implement an explicit TS-compatible framing choice with the initial header and no extra result record, while documenting any retained native summary mode and exit-code differences. Ensure repeated mode invocation cannot duplicate listeners and slow output cannot grow an unbounded queue.
entries.priority_reason: Wire compatibility, final-event delivery and a retained unbounded watch affect script correctness and long-running or embedded reuse.

entries.title: HTML export assembly, theme projection and file output
entries.what: Create a self-contained HTML artifact containing the complete session tree and optional runtime metadata, with the selected terminal theme projected into the viewer. Native HTML export exists, but currently renders only static escaped transcript text.
entries.mechanism:
Export assembles local viewer assets and serialized session data into one HTML file. Live-session export can include the current system prompt, tool schemas and custom tool renderings; file-only export has no live runtime metadata.

exportSessionToHtml accepts ExportOptions or an output-path string. It requires a session file path and that path to exist, throwing distinct in-memory and nothing-to-export errors. It does not require a nonempty entry array after the file existence check. Data includes header, every getEntries entry, current leafId, optional state.systemPrompt, tools projected to name/description/parameters, and nonempty custom-renderer results. ExportFromFile resolves and checks its input, opens SessionManager and includes header/all entries/leaf only; it ignores an options.toolRenderer because it never invokes custom prerendering. SESSION-038 owns the input journal format and restoration interpretation (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts:236-306).

An explicit truthy output path is normalized with the shared path helper; otherwise the name is APP_NAME+'-session-'+basename(input,'.jsonl')+'.html' in the current working directory. Both APIs write synchronously as UTF-8, overwrite an existing destination and return the path. They do not create parent directories, stage an atomic replacement, or stream large sessions. Despite async declarations, local asset/file operations are synchronous. Read/write/serialization errors propagate (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts:272-315).

generateHtml synchronously reads template.html, template.css, template.js and the bundled Marked/Highlight.js files from getExportTemplateDir. It JSON-stringifies SessionData, UTF-8/base64 encodes it and places that payload in the session-data element, preventing raw session text from terminating the script/data element. CSS placeholders are replaced in THEME_VARS/BODY_BG/CONTAINER_BG/INFO_BG order, then HTML placeholders in CSS/JS/SESSION_DATA/MARKED_JS/HIGHLIGHT_JS order. Each call is a single String.replace using replacement-string semantics, not a function replacement or global template engine. Browser assets are local inline content; no network asset fetch is necessary merely to open the artifact (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts:130-175; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.html:1-56).

Theme variables enumerate every resolved color. Explicit export page/card/info colors use nullish precedence over derived colors. The fallback source color is userMessageBg or #343541; derivation parses six-digit hex or rgb integer syntax, uses gamma-adjusted luminance with threshold 0.5, then selects light page brightness 0.96/card original/info offsets +10,+5,-20, or dark page 0.7/card 0.85/info +20,+15,+0. Components are clamped/rounded by the brightness/offset helpers, but rgb parser input itself is not range-validated. Unparseable input uses the source's fixed RGB fallbacks. TUI-004 owns palette resolution; this entry owns the additional export color derivation and template insertion (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts:18-127).

The CSS supplies a 12 px/18 px monospace viewer, a default 400 px sidebar bounded 240–840 px, an 800 px main column, a 900 px mobile layout boundary, print adjustments and exact preformatted output/ANSI-line whitespace rules. Bundled vendor headers identify Marked 18.0.5/MIT and Highlight.js 11.9.0/BSD-3-Clause; they are frozen source snapshots, not externally verified release downloads. Marked lines 38/43 were connector-redacted and remain unverified; every other vendor line and all exporter assets were read. No browser export was run.
entries.interfaces: ExportOptions {outputPath?, themeName?, toolRenderer?}; exportSessionToHtml(SessionManager, state?, options|string), exportFromFile(path, options|string)→Promise<string>. Embedded SessionData {header, entries, leafId, systemPrompt?, tools?, renderedTools?}. Files are UTF-8 HTML with inline JS/CSS/vendor assets and base64 JSON.

entries.title: Offline HTML tree navigation, filtering, deep links and download
entries.what: Let a recipient inspect branches and specific messages in a saved HTML session, search/filter the tree, copy a deep link and download the embedded journal without contacting the agent.
entries.mechanism:
The viewer reconstructs a navigable tree from the embedded entries and shows one root-to-leaf conversation path. Its browser controls operate entirely on that data, with optional metadata supplied by a containing share viewer.

Startup decodes base64 through atob→Uint8Array→TextDecoder→JSON.parse with no local catch/schema check. ice-url-params meta content takes precedence over location.search; a truthy leafId parameter wins over the embedded leaf, and targetId controls highlighting/scrolling. Entry and tool-call maps keep the last value for duplicate IDs. Label entries update labels only when both targetId and label are truthy, so a later empty label does not remove an earlier label. Null/undefined/self-parent and orphan entries become roots; children sort by numeric timestamps, roots retain source order. Parent traversal stops for missing/falsy/self parent but has no visited-ID guard, so a multi-node cycle can hang traversal. A robust native export boundary should reject or handle malformed trees instead of copying that weakness (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:8-145).

Clicking a node chooses a descendant by repeatedly following the last timestamp-sorted child; this is a local newest-child walk, not a global maximum timestamp over all leaves. Flattening prefers the active branch and recomputes indentation/connectors after filtering by attaching descendants to the nearest visible ancestor. Filters are default, no-tools, user-only, labeled-only and all. The current leaf is returned before every hide/filter/search check. Other assistant entries without nonblank text are hidden unless stopReason is truthy and neither stop nor toolUse; thus the condition also treats length as exceptional. Default excludes label/custom/model_change/thinking_level_change, no-tools also excludes toolResult, user-only requires a user message, and labeled-only requires a defined label. Search checks that every token appears in lowercased searchable text assembled from labels/roles/content and selected metadata; compaction contributes its type keyword, not the summary body. The search-token initializer at line 369 is connector-redacted, so its exact preprocessing is explicitly unverified (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:155-363; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:374-558).

Initial tree rendering constructs DOM rows/listeners; later navigation updates active classes/path markers without rebuilding the complete filtered order. Search/filter controls force a rebuild. Per-entry content DOM is cached, then cloned on navigation, so expanded/collapsed state is not persistent across branch replacement. Navigation recomputes the global header and selected path, routes a tool-result target to its call element, highlights for 2000 ms and scrolls after a zero-delay timeout. Global stats still describe all embedded entries, not just that selected branch. Invalid truthy leaf IDs can yield an empty path rather than falling back to a valid leaf (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:708-799; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1461-1551; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1853-1865).

Download reconstructs an optional header using {type:'header',...header}, followed by all entries, joins with LF without a terminal LF, creates an application/x-ndjson Blob, downloads as header.id or session plus .jsonl, then revokes the object URL. Because the spread follows type, an existing header.type wins. Deep links include leafId and targetId; an injected ice-share-base-url is concatenated with '&'+params, otherwise the current URL keeps its hash and first empty-valued query key as the gist ID. The template does not read ICE_SHARE_VIEWER_URL or upload a gist; that is a separate TUI share-command boundary. Browser copy tries navigator.clipboard.writeText then hidden-textarea execCommand('copy'), gives a 1500 ms success indicator, and can leave the textarea if the fallback throws before removal (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1069-1171).

Sidebar width persists under localStorage key ice-share:v1:sidebar-width. It starts from CSS defaults 400/min 240/max 840 (JS fallback max 720), reserves 320 px content space, clamps on resize, supports pointer drag and double-click reset, and uses a 900 px mobile query with an overlay toggle. T toggles currently rendered thinking and O tool outputs, except in editable/button targets. Escape clears search and navigates to the original leaf before the editable-element guard; it does not force a full tree rebuild in that path. Toggle booleans are not reapplied automatically to newly cloned branch content. The HTML contains image-modal markup, but this source has no corresponding image-modal activation handler; do not claim implemented image zoom (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1644-1865).
entries.interfaces: Browser query parameters leafId, targetId and first empty-valued gist key; meta ice-url-params and ice-share-base-url; localStorage ice-share:v1:sidebar-width; filters default/no-tools/user-only/labeled-only/all; T/O/Escape controls; window.downloadSessionJson. No agent RPC or network upload is performed by these controls.

MISC-017 supplies data/assets; MISC-019 supplies rendered content. SESSION-029/030/034 own the journal schema, tolerant reads and branch views. TUI-078 owns the concrete /share uploader and ICE_SHARE_VIEWER_URL; no upload mechanism or LOC is assigned to this template.

Give search preprocessing an explicit reviewed contract rather than guessing the redacted expression. Rebuild or update filtered ordering consistently on navigation, preserve intended toggle state and validate requested leaf/target IDs. Construct URLs with URL/URLSearchParams rather than blind separator concatenation; keep upload authorization in the TUI command. entries.title: HTML message, Markdown, image and built-in tool rendering
entries.what: Render the full conversation and tool results in the exported viewer while treating ordinary transcript content as data. The current TS template has useful escaping and URL checks, but one read-tool argument branch still inserts unescaped markup and must not be copied unchanged.
entries.mechanism:
The viewer renders user/assistant content, system metadata and tool activity into HTML, using Markdown only at selected content boundaries. Tool results are attached to their matching call instead of shown as separate result messages.

User text blocks join with LF. An exact anchored <skill name="..." location="..."> block with required newlines is recognized; its body uses Markdown and optional trailing user content/images render as siblings. Assistant text and thinking are rendered in a first pass, then tool calls in a second pass, so cross-type interleaving is not preserved. Thinking is initially expanded. Error/aborted messages receive error presentation. BashExecution uses a 10-line expandable output; model changes, compaction, branch summaries and displayed custom messages have distinct cards. Compaction summary text is escaped, branch/custom content uses Markdown where selected, and unsupported entry types produce no transcript card (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:321-330; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1174-1321).

findToolResult scans all embedded entries and returns the first matching toolCallId, without restricting to the active branch; the tree's separate tool-call map retains the last duplicate. Tool status is pending without a result, otherwise error/success. Built-in renderers cover exactly bash/read/write/edit/ls. Bash trims result text and previews 5 lines; read renders images then text with 10-line/file-extension syntax highlighting; write previews content 10 lines; edit uses escaped +/-/context diff lines when details.diff is truthy; ls previews 20. Generic/custom fallback shows escaped JSON arguments and 10-line text. File path inputs accept file_path then path; invalid nonstring values receive visible placeholders. Tabs become three spaces. Syntax failure falls back to escaped text. Read-tool images are data URIs with escaped MIME/data fields, but this branch has no separate MIME allowlist (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:799-1063).

Source-proven TS defect: the read renderer escapes the file path, but when a path is non-null and offset or limit is defined, it inserts startLine=offset??1 directly into the line-number span. There is no numeric validation or HTML escaping on offset at that boundary; a malformed saved/model tool-call argument can insert markup when that card is rendered. The computed endLine does not protect the raw startLine. The saved transcript may include rejected tool calls, so host tool-schema validation must not be assumed to sanitize every historical argument. Preserve the native escaped-data boundary when implementing this branch (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:947-958). This is static-source analysis, not a browser exploit reproduction.

escapeHtml converts &,<,>, double/single quotes. Markdown URL sanitation trims and strips C0/DEL before checking an explicit scheme; only http, https, mailto, tel, ftp are accepted when a scheme exists. Relative and protocol-relative URLs remain allowed. Rejected links retain rendered label text; rejected images become escaped alt text. Link/image attributes and inline code are escaped. Marked runs with gfm/breaks, custom strict double-tilde strikethrough, and html/tag tokenizer overrides returning undefined. The reviewed vendor use wrapper falls back only for strict false, so these overrides suppress raw-HTML token recognition; safeMarkedParse itself is just marked.parse without a catch. Code blocks use an available explicit Highlight.js language or autodetection, with escaped fallback on highlighting errors (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:607-639; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1557-1642; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/vendor/marked.min.js:75).

Pre-rendered custom HTML strings are intentionally inserted as HTML; the standard renderer produces them through escaped ANSI conversion, but arbitrary supplied ToolHtmlRenderer output is a distinct trusted interface. Global header statistics count all entries: message/tool-call/compaction/branch/custom totals, assistant usage/cost sums and encountered provider/model pairs, rather than selected-branch totals. System prompt previews 10 lines and tool schemas list property descriptions/required flags with escaped strings. Existing XSS/skill tests inspect source patterns and helper strings; they are not executed DOM tests and do not cover the unescaped offset branch (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1024-1048; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1323-1460; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/export-html-xss.test.ts:1-68; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/export-html-skill-block.test.ts:1-41).
