A renderer instance retains state for each tool-call ID and turns returned terminal component lines into escaped HTML. The export pass uses that renderer only for tools not handled directly by the browser template.

createToolHtmlRenderer receives a definition lookup, theme, cwd and width default 100. It owns separate maps for prior call components, prior result components, arbitrary state objects and arguments. renderCall caches arguments before looking up the definition, invokes renderCall with the previous call component, stores the returned component, renders at width and converts its lines. Context has toolCallId, args, cwd, shared state, lastComponent, invalidate no-op, executionStarted=true, argsComplete=true, showImages=false; call context is expanded=false, isPartial=true, isError=false. Missing definitions/renderers or any thrown error return undefined so the exporter can fall back (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/tool-renderer.ts:58-119).

renderResult passes content/details/isError as a generic tool result, renders collapsed first with isPartial=false, stores that component, then renders expanded with the just-stored collapsed component as lastComponent and the same per-call state. Both variants remove leading/trailing lines that become blank after stripping only ESC[digits/semicolons m SGR sequences and trimming. Return always includes expanded, even empty; collapsed is included only when nonempty and different. Any error in either phase returns undefined for the entire result, including a successful collapsed phase. Maps have no size bound or explicit dispose and live as long as this renderer object (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/tool-renderer.ts:44-55; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/tool-renderer.ts:121-173).

The export traversal preserves entry order. For assistant tool calls outside bash/read/write/edit/ls, a truthy call rendering creates/replaces the record for its ID. For tool results, it invokes result rendering when a prior record exists or the result's name is not one of those template-rendered tools; a truthy result object merges collapsed/expanded strings with existing call HTML. A later call with the same ID can overwrite earlier result data. The arbitrary ToolHtmlRenderer interface itself may throw and is not caught by preRenderCustomTools; only the standard created renderer has catch/fallback behavior (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts:177-230).

ansiToHtml recognizes SGR sequences matching ESC[digits/semicolons m. It tracks foreground/background, bold, dim, italic and underline, resets with 0/22/23/24/39/49 and supports 16-color,256-color and truecolor codes. Standard 16 colors use a fixed palette; indices 16–231 use the 6x6x6 cube and 232+ grayscale, without explicit range validation. Unsupported codes are ignored. Every style transition closes/opens a span; ordinary text escapes &,<,>, quotes/apostrophes. Non-SGR control sequences are not parsed as terminal state. ansiLinesToHtml resets style separately for each line, wraps each in div.ansi-line, uses   for an empty rendered line and joins with no extra source whitespace. The whitespace test asserts exact adjacent div output and trimmed custom-result margins; it was not executed (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/ansi-to-html.ts:1-259; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/export-html-whitespace.test.ts:1-43).

entries.title: Llama router requests, SSE progress and load/download completion
entries.what: Control an already running llama.cpp router and determine when model load, unload and download operations finish. OpenAI-compatible inference alone does not implement this management protocol.
entries.mechanism:
The client sends management requests to a normalized router base URL and combines server events with repeated catalog reads. Each ordinary HTTP request has a timeout, but the overall load/download/unload waits have no independent deadline.

URL normalization trims input, requires http or https, clears query/fragment, strips trailing path slashes and one terminal /v1, and removes the final slash from the serialized URL. It does not require loopback, reject URL userinfo or restrict a path prefix. llamaInferenceUrl appends /v1. request preserves supplied headers, adds application/json when body is defined, adds Bearer auth only for a truthy key and combines a 15000 ms AbortSignal.timeout with any caller signal. It attempts response.json even for failures; invalid JSON becomes undefined. Non-OK throws a nested error.message when it is a nonempty string, otherwise an HTTP-status fallback. No retry, redirect override or response byte bound is implemented (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:141-180).

GET /models optionally adds ?reload=1. The response requires data array and every member to have string id and string status.value; it does not validate status against the declared unloaded/loading/loaded/downloading/sleeping union or validate nested metadata. Load posts {model} to /models/load, unload to /models/unload, download to /models. unloadAndWait first unloads, then lists until the model is absent or exactly unloaded, sleeping 100 ms between reads. Request timeouts repeat per request and therefore do not bound the whole loop (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:182-211).

watch GETs /models/sse with optional Bearer and only its caller signal, requiring OK/body but no MIME check. It uses a nonfatal streaming TextDecoder, normalizes CRLF within each decoded chunk, splits LF-LF frames, collects only lines starting data:, trims their leading payload whitespace and joins them with LF. JSON events require string model/event. Malformed JSON and exceptions thrown by onEvent are swallowed by the same catch. There is no buffer/frame/record limit, decoder EOF flush, residual-frame processing, reader.cancel or releaseLock finally. Chunk-local CRLF normalization can miss a CR/LF split across chunks. These source weaknesses are not required properties of a native client (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:213-245).

loadAndWait starts a fire-and-forget watcher before the POST and suppresses watcher rejection. It accepts only target-model model_status/status_change events; loaded sets an eventLoaded flag and unloaded records a load error. After POST and initial progress it polls: caller abort first, catalog loaded success, then eventLoaded with missing catalog entry yields a synthetic loaded record, then failed-status/event error, then 250 ms sleep. Thus catalog loaded wins even if a failure flag was also observed. A defined exit_code selects the exit-code error message. Finally it unlinks and aborts the watcher without awaiting watcher completion. Load progress recognizes current then stage strings, replaces underscores in stage labels, clamps a numeric stage fraction to 0..1 and computes (stageIndex+fraction)/stageCount when possible; it does not explicitly reject NaN (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:86-106; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:247-286).

downloadAndWait similarly starts a watcher, tracks download_finished/download_failed/download_progress, posts the request and polls with 500 ms sleeps. Each loop checks caller abort, then an event failure, then catalog. A downloading entry sets sawDownloading and updates progress; otherwise finished or an existing entry after sawDownloading or at least 2 polls returns a final reload list. Merely seeing a non-downloading entry twice can therefore count as completion without an explicit finished event. Progress sums numeric done/total from nested progress or the supplied object, ignores nonnumeric pairs, rejects only total<=0 and reports an unclamped done/total ratio; negative/nonfinite inputs are not otherwise validated. formatBytes uses raw B below 1024, then KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB with one decimal for values>=10 and two otherwise. Finally abort/unlink does not await watch termination (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:108-139; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:288-331).

The full llama suite checks URL normalization, model mapping/auth/cache and fixture-driven SSE load/download progress. It does not prove real server compatibility, stalled-loop termination, arbitrary chunk boundaries or UI rollback; no server or test was executed.

MISC-007/SET-013 supply shared cancellation/HTTP policy where appropriate; the router's completion state machine remains specific to this client. AI-003's generic inference dispatch does not satisfy management endpoint support.
entries.rust: The reviewed native provider modules and private execution binding support model inference/custom providers, but no in-repository llama.cpp router management client or matching management endpoints were found in the recorded Rust source search (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/mod.rs:1-47; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/binding.rs:30-82). The search included llama.cpp, LLAMA_BASE_URL/LLAMA_API_KEY, /models/sse, /models/load and associated token/quantization symbols. External provider packages not present in these trees remain unverified; a generic OpenAI-compatible provider is not counted as load/unload/download parity.
entries.port: Implement a dedicated router client over the existing native HTTP policy, with typed catalog/events and exact completion branch ordering. Use a bounded streaming SSE parser that handles chunk-split CRLF/UTF-8 and always releases/cancels readers. Distinguish per-request timeout from an operation deadline and make cancellation/join ownership explicit. Validate progress numerics and reconcile event success with catalog state deliberately, documenting any stronger completion policy. Future checks should cover polling without SSE, event/catalog disagreement, missing models after loaded, failure before success, arbitrary frame splits, never-ending operations and user cancellation.

entries.title: Hugging Face token lookup, GGUF discovery and quantization grouping
entries.what: Search Hugging Face for GGUF models, identify their downloadable quantizations and report gated-access requirements before asking the llama.cpp server to download a model.
entries.mechanism:
The helper discovers an optional Hugging Face credential and queries the model API. It groups GGUF shards into quantizations, but does not download model files itself or authorize the separate router process.

findHuggingFaceToken first returns trimmed nonempty HF_TOKEN. It then checks, in order, HF_TOKEN_PATH, HF_HOME/token, XDG_CACHE_HOME/huggingface/token and homedir/.cache/huggingface/token. Falsy paths are removed and exact duplicate paths deduplicated in insertion order. Each UTF-8 file is trimmed; any read error or empty content is skipped. A supplied env map changes environment candidates but not the homedir() fallback. This is source behavior only: no real token file or user home state was accessed in the audit (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/huggingface.ts:37-61).

The client defaults to https://huggingface.co and strips trailing slashes from an injected base URL without additional URL validation. It sets Bearer auth only for a truthy token and combines a 15000 ms timeout with a caller signal. It attempts JSON parse, tolerates parse failure as undefined until the caller validates shape, and throws a nonempty top-level error string or status fallback. HTTP429 uses Number(retry-after) or a ratelimit substring matching start/semicolon followed immediately by t=digits; it emits a retry-in-seconds hint only when the chosen number is truthy. It performs no wait/retry and does not parse HTTP-date Retry-After (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/huggingface.ts:26-35; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/huggingface.ts:63-98).

Search GETs /api/models with search=query, filter=gguf, sort=downloads, direction=-1, limit=20. It requires an array, filters out nonobject/nonstring-id entries, preserves returned order and gives downloads 0 unless the field is typeof number; finiteness/integer validation is absent. Details encodes each slash-separated ID segment and GETs /api/models/{id}?blobs=true. It requires an object, walks array siblings, accepts case-insensitive .gguf paths, extracts basename and excludes names beginning mmproj case-insensitively (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/huggingface.ts:100-133).

Grouping removes one terminal -ddddd-of-ddddd shard suffix, recognizes the source suffix grammar for optional UD- plus IQ/Q digit-and-underscore forms, BF16/F16/F32 or MXFP digit forms, and uppercases the quantization. It sums every numeric size for that group; any member missing numeric size makes the reported total undefined. It does not validate shard completeness, uniqueness, positive/finite byte counts or a complete numbered sequence. Q4_K_M sorts first, then known size ascending with unknown at Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, then locale name. Result id uses a string payload id else the requested ID; gated is auto/manual only, otherwise false. Fixture tests cover the token/environment preference and quantization grouping; no Hugging Face request, real token lookup or model download was performed (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/huggingface.ts:5-8; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/huggingface.ts:124-157).
entries.dependency_text: MISC-024 owns selection/gated-access presentation and MISC-021 asks the router to perform actual downloads. The discovered client token is not automatically forwarded to the router; its server environment must independently have access. SET-013 supplies shared HTTP behavior, not model-discovery semantics.
entries.rust: No matching native HF token lookup/GGUF repository query/quantization-grouping implementation was found in the recorded Rust symbol/endpoint search. The actual native provider module inventory contains inference adapters, not this model-download discovery client (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/mod.rs:1-47). Native package installers are unrelated artifact protocols and are not counted as a counterpart. External packages remain unverified.
entries.port: Add a focused Hugging Face discovery client and source-ordered token resolver, keeping client authentication separate from the router's download credentials. Bound response bodies, validate numeric sizes and shard metadata, and retain unknown totals when evidence is incomplete. Preserve query order/limit and explicit gated states. Treat rate-limit hints as data and implement any retry policy only deliberately. Future checks should cover empty/error token candidates, duplicate paths, remote result filtering, mixed-case suffixes, shard gaps/duplicates, mmproj exclusion and missing/nonfinite sizes.

entries.title: Built-in llama provider login, environment resolution and catalog publication
entries.what: Expose loaded llama.cpp router models through the ordinary provider/model interfaces, with optional API-key login and cached catalog restoration. Configuring a compatible inference URL alone does not reproduce this provider's discovery and auth rules.
entries.mechanism:
The built-in extension registers llama.cpp as a provider and maintains its current loaded-model list. Login validates the router, and catalog refresh can restore saved entries before performing permitted network work.

The built-in extension list contains one hidden llama.cpp factory. createLlamaProvider starts with an empty model array, id/name llama.cpp, OpenAI-completions API and default inference base http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1. setCatalog includes only status.value exactly loaded; sleeping is excluded even though the manager UI treats sleeping as loaded. Each model keeps its router id as id/name, uses n_ctx??n_ctx_train when truthy and >0 else 128000 as both contextWindow and maxTokens, has reasoning=false and zero costs, and adds image input only if input_modalities includes 'image'. Compat flags disable store/developer-role/reasoning-effort/strict mode, enable stream usage and choose max_tokens. Numeric metadata is not comprehensively validated here (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/index.ts:1-5; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/provider.ts:13-68).

The API-key login flow asks for text server URL with process.env.LLAMA_BASE_URL nullish placeholder/default, then selects enteredUrl.trim() || ambient LLAMA_BASE_URL || default and normalizes it. It asks for an optional secret key, trims it, and lists the router with the interaction signal before returning {type:'api_key', key:nonempty-or-undefined, env:{LLAMA_BASE_URL:serverUrl}}. A bad router therefore prevents successful credential return; persistence belongs to the generic auth host (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/provider.ts:69-93).

Auth check/resolve prefer a nonempty stored credential.env.LLAMA_BASE_URL, then ctx.env('LLAMA_BASE_URL') trimmed; no configured URL means unavailable. check returns type api_key and a source label based merely on credential object presence. resolve chooses credential.key ?? ctx.env('LLAMA_API_KEY') ?? 'local', so an explicitly empty key is retained, and returns auth {apiKey, baseUrl:normalized+'/v1'} plus merged credential environment with the normalized URL. The provider's default base URL alone does not make auth available (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/provider.ts:15-26; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/provider.ts:94-109).

refreshModels first filters stored models to provider llama.cpp and api openai-completions, then publishes only an update callback restoring them; publish=false ends refresh. Network discovery additionally requires allowNetwork, a nonaborted signal, credential.type api_key and a nonempty URL specifically in that credential's env. An environment-only auth configuration can resolve inference but does not trigger this network branch. The router list is followed by another abort check; only loaded models are published with persist {models, checkedAt:Date.now()} and an update replacing the in-memory array. There is no local catch/retry. stream/streamSimple delegate to the existing compat provider transport (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/provider.ts:112-147).

The manager's syncCatalog has a 15000 ms signal, obtains or accepts a catalog, calls setCatalog before awaiting modelRegistry.refresh restricted to llama.cpp, then throws if that refresh reports aborted or a provider error. Thus the controller array can already change before registry refresh failure. The full fixture suite covers registration, model metadata, stored/offline restoration and auth; it was not executed (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:46-62).
entries.interfaces:
Provider/API llama.cpp/openai-completions; default router http://127.0.0.1:8080; environment LLAMA_BASE_URL, LLAMA_API_KEY; optional api_key credential with env.LLAMA_BASE_URL; getModels, refreshModels, stream, streamSimple; LlamaProviderController.setCatalog. Login is the generic /login llama.cpp flow, not a /llama login subcommand.

entries.title: Interactive llama model manager, search and cancellation recovery
entries.what: Provide an interactive model manager that can inspect the router, choose load/unload behavior, search and download GGUF models, and recover previously loaded models when a replacement is cancelled.
entries.mechanism:
The /llama command opens a dedicated TUI workflow and ignores its command arguments. It coordinates router operations and user decisions; it is not a parser for load/unload/download/login subcommands.

Outside ctx.mode==='tui' the command warns and returns. It obtains generic provider auth, warns to use /login llama.cpp if absent, and constructs the router client from result.env.LLAMA_BASE_URL or auth.baseUrl. The first catalog read and every post-action read run through syncCatalog. On read failure, a Retry/Close selector loops only the read; it does not replay a failed mutation. Connection errors are Error instances whose lowercased name/message contain 'fetch failed','timeout' or 'network'. Nonconnection action errors are shown only after a successful reread, while connection-classified action errors are suppressed there. There is no additional ICE_OFFLINE check in this command flow (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:7-40; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:181-227).

The model list sorts exactly loaded first then ID locale order, displays at most 12 rows and appends the internal '\0download' action. Sleeping models are described and acted on as loaded, but do not receive the list's loaded-sort preference. Context labels use n_ctx??n_ctx_train when truthy, otherwise the first positive finite argument after --ctx-size/-c/-ctx. Confirmed unload awaits unloadAndWait then catalog sync. Loading while other loaded/sleeping models exist asks Unload all and load/Keep loaded and load/Cancel. Replace mode sequentially unloads old models before entering the target-load try block; a failure during that pre-try unload loop can leave earlier models unloaded without restoration. Within the later try/catch, cancelled or failed target load best-effort restores old models sequentially and refreshes; restoration failure preserves the original load error in catch. Cancel sends unload(target), not unloadAndWait (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:64-133; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:23-51; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:321-388).

Download finds a client HF token, opens search, parses a colon only after the first slash, fetches details and shows auto/manual gated-access guidance with Continue/Back. It explicitly tells the user the llama server needs its own authorized HF_TOKEN; the client token is not sent as a router credential. When no quantization was supplied, available options include sizes and Q4_K_M 'recommended'; an already supplied quantization is not checked against the discovered list. It asks the router to download repository[:quant], supports unload-as-cancel, then syncs the returned catalog. Detail fetch itself is not tied to a view-level cancellation signal (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:135-179).

Search trims input, requires 2 characters for a new query, debounces 500 ms and aborts the previous request. A per-view map caches by lowercase query without TTL/size bound. Responses enter the cache before checking closed/aborted/current-query state, so a stale response can populate cache while leaving the visible state untouched. Fuzzy filtering uses TUI-235 for membership but preserves original API order. Selection clamps after filtering and wraps on up/down; at most 10 centered rows show. Confirm prefers a query matching the exact owner/repository[:quant] regex over the highlighted result, and cancel closes once while clearing debounce/aborting request (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:96-274).

runWithProgress starts the operation immediately and converts success/failure into a fulfilled settlement object. It races that against the progress cancel key, then asks confirmation. A declined confirmation or already completed operation resumes/finishes normally. On confirmed stop it awaits the cancel callback first and aborts the operation controller in finally, then awaits settled and returns cancelled. If cancel itself rejects, control skips the later await/return and propagates that error; the operation's wrapped settlement remains observed. The 40-character bar clamps filled length but prints the raw rounded percentage, with no finite-number guard. showLlamaUi routes run completion to done and errors to notify then done; view content replacement clears the old progress resolver without settling an abandoned progress promise (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:305-319; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:419-543).

The doc's router setup flags, filesystem examples and server token guidance were read as documentation only. Existing llama tests exercise provider/client fixtures, not this complete UI recovery/cancellation flow. No model server, download, token file or test was invoked.

entries.title: Single-pass HTML entity decoding at the syntax adapter boundary
entries.what: Decode the small entity vocabulary emitted by the TS syntax highlighter once, without treating it as a browser HTML parser. Native syntax highlighting starts from plain source text and does not require this intermediate HTML decoding layer.
entries.mechanism:
The helper turns a recognized entity into text and tells its caller how many input characters to consume. The syntax adapter applies it only when its current input character is an ampersand, so decoded text is appended once rather than recursively reparsed.

decodeHtmlEntity recognizes the exact lowercase names amp, lt, gt, quot and apos. A '#x' or '#X' prefix selects Number.parseInt with radix 16; any other '#' prefix selects radix 10. The parsed number must be an integer from zero through 0x10ffff inclusive, otherwise the function returns undefined. parseInt accepts a valid numeric prefix and does not require the entire suffix to be numeric. Zero and values in the surrogate interval are not explicitly rejected: String.fromCodePoint permits a surrogate code unit in a JS string. The host-plus-Gondolin pattern says built-in read/write/edit/bash/grep/find/ls and user '!' commands are routed to a local VM with cwd mounted at /workspace. The OpenShell recipe requires a selected active gateway, describes local Docker/Podman/VM or remote Kubernetes hosting, and places built-in tools, user shell commands and extension tools inside the whole-process boundary. Remote gateways do not automatically bind-mount the local project; the guide uses clone or explicit upload/download. Its inference.local route relies on gateway-side credential injection and compatible endpoint configuration. entries.title: Local Claude SDK client configuration and private bridge credentials
entries.what: Read a dedicated local-bridge configuration and credential without importing Claude OAuth state or allowing a remote endpoint to receive the bridge token.
entries.mechanism:
The adapter accepts a narrowly defined loopback endpoint and a private token file. Configuration and token validation happen before inference, independently of the ordinary provider API-key store.

validateClientConfig first requires a non-null, non-array object and string baseUrl, then parses it with URL. It requires version===1, parsed protocol http:, hostname 127.0.0.1, pathname '/', no username/password/query/fragment, and a nonempty parsed port. These are checks on URL's normalized representation, not a raw-text URL allowlist: an explicitly default HTTP port may normalize away and fail the port check. No default service port is supplied by production code; 20129 is a test fixture. tokenFile must be a string absolute according to the platform path implementation. models must be an array of 1–32 strings matching /^claude-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,96}$/; duplicates are not rejected. The returned configuration uses url.origin and only version/baseUrl/tokenFile/models; unknown properties are discarded (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:30-65).

readPrivate opens with O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW, obtains metadata through the opened handle, and requires a regular file, reported size no greater than 65536 bytes, no group/other permission bits (mode & 0077 equals zero), and stat.uid equal to process.getuid?.(). It then reads UTF-8 and closes in finally. The same routine protects configuration JSON and the bridge token. The size check precedes readFile rather than bounding ingestion, so a concurrent file growth is not ruled out. O_NOFOLLOW applies at open according to the platform; this is not a proof that every ancestor path is a nonsymlink. There is no portable ownership fallback when getuid is unavailable. JSON parse/open/stat/read/close failures propagate to the caller (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:66-79).

The constructor validates a supplied configuration again. Its default token reader reads tokenFile privately and trims outer whitespace; an injected reader is not automatically trimmed. token() accepts exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Tokens are read for each request/status/close rather than cached in public model metadata. No fallback to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, a Claude OAuth file, or another provider is implemented in this adapter. The URL-validation test rejects remote HTTPS, localhost spelling, credentials, nonroot paths, query strings and missing ports; it does not execute a permission/ownership matrix.
entries.interfaces: BridgeClientConfig = {version:1, baseUrl:string, tokenFile:string, models:string[]}. Production extension path is <getAgentDir()>/claude-sdk.json. Private-file metadata limit is 65536 bytes; token grammar is /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/. No new environment variable or default bridge port exists here. Both configuration and token are inputs only; this module writes neither file.
entries.dependency_text: SET-001 supplies the agent directory. A separately operated local Claude SDK bridge must provision this version-1 configuration and token; its implementation and actual authentication were outside the authorized source trees.
entries.rust: Native ExecutionBinding already separates private request auth/headers from public descriptors and restores the bound model by provider/API/id before execution (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/binding.rs:30-82). Native Api::Other(String) and string ProviderId allow a claude-sdk identity; adding a hardcoded enum variant is unnecessary (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/types.rs:419-479). No local Claude SDK configuration reader, private bridge-token file contract or exact loopback service client was found in the repository-wide source search and concrete provider/extension registration paths reviewed for this fragment. Ordinary native credentials and direct Anthropic HTTP support are different protocols.

Preserve the loopback/authentication boundary and prevent public model metadata from carrying the secret. Define portable ownership behavior explicitly. Enforce the file limit during reading if strengthening the pre-read metadata check, and document that improvement rather than claiming the TS reader is race-proof. Keep existing private execution bindings. Verify config shape, normalized URL edge cases, duplicate model policy, private-file limits and token rotation during future implementation work.

entries.title: Claude SDK session-handle isolation, reuse and cache limits
entries.what: Keep distinct ICE sessions from sharing a native bridge conversation, reuse an acknowledged handle for continuation, and reject a concurrent request for the same local session key.
entries.mechanism:
The client stores bridge handles separately from the public ICE session identifier. Each instance owns its own map and active-key set, so a request can continue only that instance's acknowledged session.

HandleState is {handle, wireSessionId, touched}; handles is a Map<string, HandleState>, active is a Set<string>, and instance is a constructor-time random UUID. A request uses options.sessionId ?? randomUUID() as its local key and !options.sessionId as its temporary flag. Thus an empty string is a real local key but still receives temporary cleanup. Before reading the token or looking up a handle, the request rejects an already active key; otherwise it adds the key and records locked=true. A conflicting second request does not remove the first request's key or cancel its handle because locked remains false on that path (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:252-277).

After token acquisition, the client walks cached handles in insertion order. It deletes and best-effort cancels an entry only if the key is not active and Date.now()-touched is strictly greater than 10*60000 ms. This is opportunistic cleanup during a later stream call, not a timer. touched is set when ready is received, not when the turn finishes. Because the current key was already marked active, its own old handle is not expired by this sweep and can be reused; server-side session_lost may then fail it. Cleanup cancellations are awaited sequentially. The gate rejects a new key when handles.size>=64, but it does not reserve a slot before awaiting inference. Concurrent different new keys can therefore pass the same pre-ready size check and later exceed 64 cached handles; do not call this a strict global concurrency/capacity bound (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:277-287).

An existing key supplies its previous wireSessionId and handle. A new one uses instance + ':' + a new UUID; every request also gets a fresh requestId. A validated ready record creates/replaces the local HandleState using that wireSessionId, the server's 64-hex handle and the current time. A turn record must match the most recently accepted handle. On a locked request failure the local key is deleted; selected handles are cancelled best-effort. Finally the active key is released, and temporary requests delete/cancel selected handles even after success. No handle map is persisted, reconstructed from saved chat history, or replayed after loss. The two-session test confirms distinct wire IDs and reuse of the first session's original handle; it does not exercise the parallel new-key capacity race.
entries.interfaces: Local key options.sessionId; wire {sessionId, requestId, handle?}; HandleState {handle:string, wireSessionId:string, touched:number}; 64-entry admission check; inactive TTL strictly greater than 600000 ms since ready. Wire handle syntax is 64 lowercase hex characters. Maps are in-memory and scoped to one ClaudeSdkClient instance.
entries.dependency_text: MISC-030 authenticates the client and MISC-037 owns best-effort cancellation/error completion. MISC-033 consumes the private wire identity produced here. External bridge handle validity, TTL and changed-tool-context rejection are not provable from this client repository alone.
entries.rust: Native PluggableProvider owns an extension registry snapshot and library lifetime, and clones model/context/options into each spawned request (rust:crates/ice-extensions/src/provider.rs:80-201). That is real native request ownership, but it does not implement local-key-to-wire-handle reuse, this bridge's ready handshake, per-key exclusion or TTL/capacity state. No matching Claude SDK handle registry was found in the audited provider paths.
entries.port: Add a per-provider client state object with isolated local-to-wire mappings and cancellation ownership. Use an explicit lock/reservation policy so concurrent new sessions cannot overrun the intended capacity, and decide whether a current stale key should be expired before reuse. Preserve no automatic replay after session loss. Keep correlation state private and out of transcript persistence. Future checks should cover empty versus absent session IDs, same-key rejection without cancelling the owner, rotating ready handles, exact TTL origin/boundary, parallel capacity admission and shutdown racing a ready event.
entries.priority_reason: Handle isolation and honest lifecycle bounds prevent cross-session continuation and accidental replay of tool-bearing conversations.

entries.title: Claude SDK request projection, protected envelope and output authority
entries.what: Send the real ICE prompt, conversation and tool schemas to the local bridge while preventing a payload hook from changing authenticated session identity or widening the caller's output ceiling.
entries.mechanism:
The adapter projects the existing conversation into a versioned bridge request. A payload hook may customize ordinary content, but correlation fields and the upper output limit are checked again before any inference request.

The model id must be in config.models. Truthy deferred, any defined temperature, a toolChoice other than undefined/'auto'/'none', and a samplingParams object with own enumerable keys are rejected before inference. Forced tool choices are explicitly unsupported, including 'required', 'any' and a tool selector object. Unsupported options are not silently translated. The initial cap is Math.min(options.maxTokens ?? 16384, options.hardMaxOutputTokens ?? 128000,128000), and must be an integer at least 1. This uses the caller options, not model.maxTokens or contextWindow; those published values are not an additional local context/input bound (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:268-288).

The payload is {version:1, requestId, sessionId, handle? , model, systemPrompt, messages, tools, thinking?, maxTokens}. systemPrompt defaults only nullish input to ''. User and assistant messages retain role/content; tool-result messages retain role/toolCallId/toolName/content/isError. Other timestamps, provider/model/usage metadata are omitted. Tool declarations retain exact name/description/parameters without schema conversion; toolChoice='none' sends an empty array, otherwise context.tools defaults empty. A truthy reasoning value is sent as thinking, including a truthy string 'off'. This module neither rewrites the identity in the prompt nor executes tools (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:80-91; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:289-307).

onPayload is awaited with (payload, model); nullish return preserves the current payload. Its result must be a non-array object, and version/requestId/sessionId/handle/model must remain exactly equal to their reserved values. A changed protected field produces session_conflict. A defined maxTokens must be a finite number; it is clamped to the original cap, or reset to cap when omitted. The post-hook path does not repeat integer/positive validation, so finite negative or fractional hook values can survive; a native port should repair that contract hole. Messages/tools/systemPrompt may be replaced, but later returned-tool membership is checked against original context.tools, not the hook's replacement list. JSON.stringify output must fit 8*1024*1024 UTF-8 bytes (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:308-326).

Only after these checks does the adapter push start and POST /api/services/claude-sdk/step with Bearer auth, Content-Type application/json, Accept application/x-ndjson, redirect:error and the request abort signal. options.fetch overrides this step call only. onResponse receives {status, headers:Object.fromEntries(...)} and model before HTTP status validation; a throwing hook fails the request. HTTP 401 maps to unauthorized and other non-OK statuses to upstream. There is no retry, alternate provider, direct OAuth or API fallback. The read tests verify unchanged prompt/schema forwarding, protected envelope rejection, hard-cap restoration, toolChoice none and forced-choice rejection.
entries.interfaces: POST /api/services/claude-sdk/step; envelope fields and protected fields above. Default output cap 16384, default hard cap/absolute ceiling 128000, serialized request ceiling 8388608 bytes. Hooks onPayload(payload, model) and onResponse({status, headers}, model); per-request custom fetch applies only to step. entries.title: Claude SDK NDJSON framing, UTF-8 decoding and ingestion limits
entries.what: Decode the bridge response incrementally, reject malformed or truncated streams and enforce exact response-size and record-count limits before trusting a terminal turn.
entries.mechanism:
The response is a newline-delimited stream of JSON objects. The reader validates UTF-8 and framing while data arrives, and the caller accepts a final turn only after the body ends cleanly.

iterateRecords requires a body and a Content-Type value whose text starts with the case-sensitive prefix application/x-ndjson. It does not parse a MIME token or require an exact media type, so a longer value sharing that prefix is accepted. It acquires a reader and a fatal UTF-8 TextDecoder, tracks actual incoming byteLength across chunks, and rejects when total wire bytes exceed 8*1024*1024. Decoding is streaming, so UTF-8 code points and JSON syntax may cross arbitrary chunk boundaries. No Content-Length declaration substitutes for the observed-byte count (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:115-129).

Each LF-terminated line is removed from the buffer. The constant MAX_LINE_BYTES is 3*1024*1024, but the actual comparisons use JavaScript string.length, so the per-line and residual-buffer limits are UTF-16 code units, not bytes. Every complete line increments count, including blank lines, and count>65536 fails. Nonblank lines are JSON.parse'd and must be non-null non-array objects through record(); blank/whitespace-only lines are skipped. The buffer is checked after extracting all complete lines. This reader therefore has one actual wire-byte bound plus decoded-code-unit bounds, not two byte bounds (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:130-138).

At EOF decoder.decode() flushes or rejects an incomplete UTF-8 sequence. Any remaining non-whitespace buffer is a truncated frame, even if it is otherwise valid JSON; trailing whitespace without LF is allowed. Finally it awaits reader.cancel(), suppresses cancellation failure, then releases the reader lock. That cleanup await is not separately time-bounded by this generator. readRecords simply collects all yielded objects into an array; inference consumes iterateRecords directly. The stream caller rejects missing ready/terminal, unsupported event order and any record after a terminal turn, rather than treating the first successful turn as permission to ignore trailing corruption (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:140-150; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:349-379).

The malformed-stream loop tests no-ready, duplicate-terminal, truncated JSON-without-LF and bad JSON. The UTF-8 test sends one byte per chunk and verifies decoded Unicode. Neither test was executed, and no exhaustive memory bound on parsed object expansion is claimed merely from the wire limit.
entries.interfaces: Response Content-Type prefix application/x-ndjson; UTF-8 with fatal decoding; LF records; object-only JSON; actual wire ceiling 8388608 bytes; decoded line/buffer ceiling 3145728 UTF-16 code units; at most 65536 LF-terminated lines including blanks. Exported iterateRecords(Response) async generator and readRecords(Response) collector.
entries.dependency_text: This is the bridge-specific framing primitive. It is consumed by MISC-035/036/037 and is distinct from the binary/CBOR and JSONL control protocols documented under RPC.
entries.rust: Native built-in HTTP providers implement their own Anthropic/OpenAI transports and use a shared AssistantMessage event channel; concrete provider modules are listed in rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/mod.rs:8-17 and event delivery in rust:crates/ice-ai/src/event_stream.rs:18-172. No in-tree local Claude SDK NDJSON reader implements this Content-Type check, framing/count/UTF-8 policy or terminal-body validation. Existing RPC framing is a different wire protocol and must not be relabeled as SDK transport parity.
entries.port: Add an incremental bounded NDJSON decoder for the bridge with explicit byte, decoded-string and line-count units. Decide whether to preserve the permissive media-type prefix or require the parsed exact type; record any strengthening. Preserve clean EOF validation and object-only records. Use bounded accumulation and cancellation-safe reader cleanup, without calling a timeout a proof that every foreign reader finishes. Future checks should cover split multibyte characters, malformed UTF-8 at EOF, blank-line limits, nonobject JSON, exact boundaries, CRLF, whitespace-only tail and a second record after terminal.
entries.priority_reason: A bridge response must not silently truncate, accept trailing corruption or evade documented ingestion limits.

entries.title: Claude SDK terminal-turn validation and retained tool authority
entries.what: Accept only correlated, structurally valid assistant turns and known tool names from the external bridge, then return those calls to ICE for normal execution.
entries.mechanism:
The bridge can propose assistant content and tool calls, but it cannot execute tools through this adapter. A complete correlated turn must pass content, stop-reason, tool-membership and usage checks before any tool-call events are emitted.

The first successful handshake is a ready record with version===1, transport==='claude-agent-sdk', billing==='external' and a string handle matching exactly 64 lowercase hex characters. A second ready fails. text_delta and turn require readiness, and turn.handle must equal the accepted handle. An error record can appear before readiness and is mapped through the safe code table. Any unsupported event or any subsequent record after a turn fails. A terminal turn is required after clean body EOF; terminal.message must be an object (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:349-380).

content must be an array of at most 512 blocks. Text requires a string text. Thinking requires a string thinking; a defined thinkingSignature must be a string, and only redacted===true is retained. ToolCall requires name matching /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$/, a nonempty string id no longer than 256 UTF-16 code units, and non-null/non-array object arguments. IDs have no further character grammar here. Unsupported block types fail. These checks do not validate tool arguments against the declared JSON Schema or limit each argument object's depth independently of the wire reader (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:93-114).

stopReason must be stop, length or toolUse. toolUse must be equivalent to the presence of one or more tool calls; duplicate call IDs fail. Every returned name must occur in original context.tools, and toolChoice='none' rejects every returned call even if a malformed bridge ignores the empty outgoing tools array. Membership uses original context rather than a replacement tool list from onPayload. The adapter never calls a tool executor; the ordinary agent receives validated toolCall blocks and retains permission/execution authority. Empty content with stop/length is structurally allowed (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:381-390).

Usage requires object fields input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite, each a finite number between 0 and Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER inclusive. Despite the helper name positive, zero and fractions are accepted; the helper does not require integers. totalTokens is their unchecked sum, which can exceed the safe-integer bound even when each input passed. All cost fields remain zero because billing is external. The published model costs and bridge billing label do not prove free usage. Native implementation should choose exact checked numeric types rather than inheriting these TS validation weaknesses. Tests preserve signed thinking, reject unknown tools and enforce toolChoice none; they were read only.
entries.interfaces: Ready {type:'ready', version:1, handle, transport:'claude-agent-sdk', billing:'external'}; Turn {type:'turn', handle, message:{content, stopReason, usage}}. Content variants text/thinking/toolCall with exact requirements above. Stop reasons stop|length|toolUse. Usage input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite are required; computed totalTokens and zero costs are local output fields.
entries.dependency_text: MISC-034 supplies clean framing and MISC-033 request/tool context. AI-012 owns general tool-schema validation; this adapter's shape/name check does not replace the host's normal schema and authority checks. Server SDK behavior and tool-context correlation beyond the echoed handle are external and unverified.
entries.rust: The native Provider trait already returns assistant events to the normal agent, and PluggableProvider adapts a native plugin's streaming or terminal output into that channel (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/provider.rs:149-175; rust:crates/ice-extensions/src/provider.rs:151-201). That preserves a viable host architecture. No dedicated Claude SDK ready/turn protocol, external-billing assertion, original-tool-name membership check or wire usage validator is present in the inspected transport set. A native SDK provider must implement those boundary checks while retaining existing tool execution ownership.
entries.port: Implement typed ready/turn/content decoding and validate the full terminal before releasing tool-call events. Preserve original-context tool membership and no-tools authority; then use normal native schema/permission/execution checks. Use bounded integer usage values and checked accumulation if repairing the TS numeric weakness. Preserve signatures and redacted thinking flags without identity rewriting. Future verification should include duplicate handles/ready/terminal, unknown tools, duplicate/oversized IDs, toolUse equivalence, empty content, fractional/overflowing usage and hook-modified tool lists.
entries.priority_reason: An external bridge must not inject unauthorized or uncorrelated tool calls into the host agent.

entries.title: Claude SDK preview streaming, stable block indices and final reconciliation
entries.what: Display incremental bridge text before the final turn while preserving exact block indices and refusing to associate a preview with a later or different content block.
entries.mechanism:
Preview text is provisional until the final turn is validated. The adapter reconciles that preview only with the first final text block, then emits any remaining blocks in their original order.

stream immediately returns an AssistantMessageEventStream and starts run asynchronously. Its output message starts with role assistant, requested model/API/provider, empty content, zero usage/cost, stopReason stop, a wall-clock timestamp and a diagnostic {type:'claude-agent-sdk', timestamp, details:{billing:'external', identityRewriting:false}}. start is pushed only after request validation/serialization and before the step fetch, so early rejected options can produce error without start (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:226-251; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:327-338).

After ready, each text_delta requires a string and appends to previewText. Buffer.byteLength(previewText)>2*1024*1024 fails. The first preview delta, including an empty string, creates text block 0 and emits text_start at index 0. Every delta replaces output.content with the accumulated first text block and emits text_delta with that index. These are mutable partial-output references in the TS adapter, not independently cloned snapshots. A later validation failure can leave previously delivered preview text visible; no rollback event is issued. Tool-call events have not yet been emitted at this stage (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:363-373).

After the entire terminal passes MISC-035 validation, a started preview requires blocks[0] to be text and its final text to start with the exact preview string. A preview is never retroactively assigned to a later text block after thinking or a tool call. output.content is set to the complete first text block; any missing suffix is emitted as one text_delta using the UTF-16 prefix length, followed by text_end. Since the prefix comparison is exact, that suffix boundary follows the original preview string. Remaining blocks begin at index 1, preserving mixed text/thinking/text order (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:399-414).

Without a preview, or for later blocks, each text block emits start/delta/end, thinking emits thinking_start/thinking_delta/thinking_end, and a toolCall emits toolcall_start then toolcall_end without an intermediate argument-delta event. The block is appended before its event sequence, so contentIndex is the current output length before append. Finally done carries the validated stop reason and full message. The mixed-block hardening test clones events and expects text indices 0 and 2 with thinking at 1; another rejects a preview whose text belongs only to a later block. Streaming tests hold the final record back, confirm early text and no duplicate suffix, and ensure an inconsistent preview emits no toolcall_end. These were read, not run.
entries.interfaces: Incoming {type:'text_delta', delta:string}; preview ceiling 2097152 UTF-8 bytes. Outgoing start, text_start/text_delta/text_end, thinking_start/thinking_delta/thinking_end, toolcall_start/toolcall_end and done with contentIndex. Diagnostic type claude-agent-sdk, billing external, identityRewriting false. No toolcall_delta is synthesized by this adapter.
entries.dependency_text: MISC-034 supplies framed records and MISC-035 the validated terminal. AI-003 owns shared provider/event-stream interfaces; existing native owned partial snapshots should be retained.
entries.rust: Native event streams already provide terminal latching, one-shot results and a RecvError if the producer disappears without a terminal result (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/event_stream.rs:18-172). Native concrete-provider events carry owned message snapshots rather than depending on this adapter's mutable output object. No Claude SDK preview-to-first-block reconciliation or exact event translation exists in the inspected provider implementation set. The gap is the bridge mapper, not a missing generic streaming channel.
entries.port: Build the bridge mapper on the existing native event stream. Preserve exact first-block reconciliation and do not release tool-call events before terminal validation. Retain owned partial snapshots and producer-drop errors. Track preview byte length incrementally to avoid repeatedly recounting a growing string if useful, while keeping the same limit semantics. Future checks should cover empty first delta, mixed block indices, a nontext first block, final suffix extension, inconsistent preview, terminal corruption after a visible preview and no duplicate terminal event.
entries.priority_reason: Correct streaming indices and reconciliation prevent duplicated text or tool events derived from an invalid final response.

entries.title: Claude SDK cancellation, safe failures and shutdown limits
entries.what: Abort a bridge request, invalidate its local continuation state and report a safe failure without reflecting arbitrary remote text or replaying the conversation through another provider.
entries.mechanism:
Each request owns an abort controller and a fixed cleanup path. Failures discard its local handle and produce one terminal error, while best-effort bridge cancellation remains distinct from proof that external work stopped.

The timer starts near the beginning of run with Math.min(options.timeoutMs ?? 600000,600000); there is no explicit lower-bound, integer or finiteness validation of timeoutMs. The caller's abort event triggers the same controller, and a pre-aborted signal is checked before active-key acquisition or network inference. The controller signal is passed to step fetch, but token reads, onPayload/onResponse and reader cleanup are not independently raced against a deadline. Consequently the timer requests cancellation rather than guaranteeing every await and external operation finishes within 600000 ms (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:252-276; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:328-342).

cancelHandle sends POST /api/services/claude-sdk/cancel with Bearer token, JSON {version:1, sessionId:wireSessionId, handle}, redirect:error and AbortSignal.timeout(2000). It uses global fetch rather than the custom inference fetch. It ignores HTTP status/body and suppresses fetch failures; success is not an acknowledgement that SDK work or descendants have ended. The comment names server TTL and disconnected-request deadline as final guards, but those are external server assumptions, not verified client guarantees. close snapshots current handles, clears the map, tries to reread a token, and concurrently cancels all captured states. Token failure returns after the map is already cleared. close does not abort/join active request controllers; an in-flight ready event can repopulate the map after the snapshot. session_shutdown awaiting close therefore does not by itself establish an empty/finished active set (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:182-205; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/extension.ts:33-35).

On failure, only the request that acquired its key deletes that handle and cancels selected state. If token acquisition failed before selected was populated, an existing cached key is deleted without a cancellation handle. The output stopReason is aborted only when the local controller is aborted, otherwise error. Local abort uses the fixed cancelled-or-timed-out message. SafeBridgeFailure exposes only predefined safe text; other exceptions become a generic transport/validation message. Remote error.message is ignored. The code table covers subscription_required, unauthorized, session_lost, session_conflict, tool_protocol, capacity, unsupported, timeout and upstream; unknown codes use upstream. A server timeout code can therefore yield reason error when the local controller did not abort. There is no provider/API fallback or automatic replay after session loss (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:152-165; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:374-377; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:431-442).

Finally the timer/listener are removed, the owning active key is released, temporary selected handles are deleted/cancelled and stream.end is called. A temporary failed request with selected state can call cancel once in catch and again in finally; each is best-effort and separately has a 2000 ms signal. The pre-abort test expects zero inference calls. The server-error test's fixture and one assertion contain connector-redacted text at lines 88/90, so those lines are excluded; visible assertions and implementation establish the fixed code-message/fallback policy without reconstructing the hidden literal. No bridge, login, SDK process or cancellation was executed.
entries.interfaces: POST /api/services/claude-sdk/cancel {version:1, sessionId, handle}; default/maximum requested deadline 600000 ms; cancellation signal 2000 ms; caller AbortSignal; close()→Promise<void>. Safe error-code enum above; terminal reason aborted|error. No retry/replay endpoint, persistent handle recovery or direct OAuth/API fallback is provided.
entries.dependency_text: MISC-030 authenticates cancellation and MISC-034 owns response reader cleanup. AI-006 supplies the shared cancellation option contract. External server TTL, disconnected-request cleanup and official SDK process termination are unverified outside these repositories.
entries.rust: Native SimpleStreamOptions has a CancellationToken and native streaming plugins latch cancellation while retaining the plugin library/context for a detached blocking request (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/provider.rs:31-54; rust:crates/ice-extensions/src/provider.rs:461-552). Those lifetime protections should be retained. They do not implement this local bridge's cancel endpoint, safe error-code table, cache invalidation or no-replay policy. No native SDK bridge client was found in the examined provider/module/registration sources.
entries.port: Implement explicit per-request cancellation ownership and safe protocol errors, keeping local cancellation separate from server acknowledgement. Strengthen shutdown with active-request tracking and joining/cancelling where the external protocol allows it; do not claim a best-effort POST proves process completion. Validate timeout inputs, avoid duplicate cleanup calls and retain enough state to cancel cached handles after credential-read failure when feasible. Preserve no replay/fallback after tool-bearing session loss. Future verification should cover same-key conflict, pre-abort, stuck hooks/readers, invalid token during close, close racing ready, server timeout without local abort, and cancellation failures.
entries.priority_reason: Cancellation must preserve handle ownership and safe failure semantics without replaying uncertain tool effects.

entries.title: Evaluation runner, explicit model defaults and separate test configuration
entries.source:
ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:1-98; ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:28-56; ice:packages/evals/package.json:1-21; ice:packages/evals/vitest.config.ts:1-21; ice:packages/evals/vitest.test.config.ts:1-15; ice:vitest.base.ts:1-29; ice:package.json:37; ice:packages/evals/test/ice-harness.test.ts:1-35; rust:Cargo.toml:1-24; rust:crates/ice-harness/Cargo.toml:1-43.

entries.what: A separate eval command chooses a default provider/model, launches only model-backed eval files, and keeps local unit tests distinct from those potentially authenticated runs.
entries.mechanism:
The runner gives explicit CLI provider/model values precedence over environment defaults and forwards other arguments to Vitest. A harness may override that default with its own model. The runner and harness validate selection at different points, so launching without a default is allowed only when the executed harnesses supply their own models.

The root npm eval script forwards to the private @zykairotis/ice-evals workspace. run-evals.mjs accepts --provider value, --model value and their = forms; repeated values overwrite earlier values. Separate-form values must be nonempty and must not start with '-'. After trimming, the presence of either CLI selector requires both CLI values; a missing CLI half is not filled from the environment. Without any CLI selector, trimmed ICE_PROVIDER and ICE_MODEL must either both exist or both be absent. All other arguments are retained in encounter order. There is no special end-of-options escape in this parser, so recognized selectors after a literal '--' are still consumed (ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:16-63).

ICE_EVAL_ARTIFACT_DIR is resolved relative to the package root when truthy; otherwise the runner creates .eval/<ISO timestamp with colons replaced>_<UUID>. It creates the directory recursively with requested mode 0700, prints the selected default and artifact location, then invokes process.execPath with Vitest's installed vitest.mjs, 'run', '--config', 'vitest.config.ts' and forwarded arguments. cwd is the eval package, stdio is inherited and the environment is copied with the resolved artifact path. Both model defaults are installed together or both removed. Spawn errors are thrown; a null child status becomes exit 1, otherwise the child status is propagated. The runner does not parse authentication or independently resolve the chosen model (ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:8-15; ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:65-98).

resolveModelSelection uses explicitModel.provider/id via nullish fallback to environment fields, then trims and requires both. An explicit empty string therefore rejects rather than falling back. The local test suite covers explicit precedence, trimming and incomplete selections; it does not execute the runner or a model. Eval configuration runs src/**/*.eval.ts in Node with fileParallelism=false, testTimeout120000, hookTimeout30000, the eval afterEach setup, the external vitest-evals reporter and the local reporter. The separate unit-test configuration selects test/**/*.test.ts. Both use the monorepo source aliases, with an explicit coding-agent index alias; package metadata pins vitest-evals 0.15.0 and Vitest 4.1.9. Compiler configuration is noEmit/NodeNext through the shared strict ES2022 base. These are source configuration facts, not an assertion that dependencies were installed or tests ran.
entries.interfaces: Command: root npm run eval -- [--provider P --model M] [Vitest arguments]. Environment: ICE_PROVIDER, ICE_MODEL, ICE_EVAL_ARTIFACT_DIR. createIceCodingAgentHarness({name?, model?:{provider, id}, noTools?, transformSystemPrompt?, output?}); default harness name ice-coding-agent. Paths: packages/evals/.eval/<timestamp>_<UUID>, runner override resolved relative to package root, src/**/*.eval.ts, test/**/*.test.ts.
entries.dependency_text: Model catalog lookup and authentication are performed later by MISC-041 through AI-002 and SESSION-028. This entry owns eval-only command/default selection rather than the normal CLI's model parser.
entries.rust: The native workspace and ice-harness crate are real Rust runtime/test packages, but their inspected manifests contain no eval package/target or wrapper for these model defaults, selectors and artifact runner. The bounded full crate search for createIceCodingAgentHarness, vitest-evals, ICE_EVAL_ and comparative eval/report names found no implementation. This is absence of the described eval runner in the inspected repository surface, not absence of native tests or a statement about external tooling. Native deterministic tests are credited in MISC-041 and MISC-048. Native comparison source: `rust:Cargo.toml:1-24`; `rust:crates/ice-harness/Cargo.toml:1-43`.
entries.port: Add an explicit opt-in eval executable or developer command with the exact selector precedence, forwarding, child exit and artifact-directory contract. Reuse the existing model/auth catalog, expose the final selected provider/model to each harness and keep deterministic tests separate from model-backed suites. Reproduce the checked-in runner's pair validation and explicit-empty behavior; if a native command adopts conventional '--' parsing, record that deliberate compatibility difference. Port the four source-read model-selection cases and add future runner tests for equals/separate forms, partial CLI selection and child failures.
entries.priority_reason: Required to run repeatable opt-in model evaluations without conflating them with ordinary unit tests.

entries.title: Isolated eval-session construction, prompt transformation and sequential reload steps
entries.what: Each harness run creates a fresh temporary project, agent directory and persistent session, then executes a string prompt or ordered prompt/reload program with a selectable output projection.
entries.mechanism:
Every run uses a fresh session and workspace while retaining the application's normal model authentication path. Optional prompt transformation sees the complete initial system prompt and is applied through a resource reload. Prompt and reload steps then execute sequentially, and the output callback sees the live final session before cleanup.

The timer and initial abort check precede model selection. ModelRuntime.create() is called with its normal defaults before the temporary root exists; getModel(provider, id) must return a model or the run rejects with 'Eval model not found: provider/id'. Only then does mkdtemp create an ice-eval- directory under the OS temp directory. workspace and agent children are created in parallel. createAgentSessionServices receives cwd, agentDir, that model runtime and SettingsManager.inMemory(); it does not replace normal model credentials with a temporary credential store. A resourceLoader systemPromptOverride closure is installed only when a transform was supplied. SessionManager.create uses the workspace and a sibling sessions directory, and its session ID is immediately placed in the 'runId' artifact. createAgentSessionFromServices selects the resolved model, thinkingLevel='off', and forwards noTools without changing its schema (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:115-151).

The transform callback is synchronous and receives evalSession.systemPrompt. Its returned string must have a nonempty trim; the original returned string, including intentional whitespace, remains the override. evalSession.reload() applies it. The harness then rejects any nonempty initial extension-path list, which asserts starting isolation before the test can create resources. It does not assert that the entire environment or model credential state is empty (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:153-168).

A string input becomes one prompt step; array steps retain order. Prompt steps call the stricter completion adapter in MISC-043. Every other branch in the typed prompt/reload union invokes reload; there is no additional runtime discriminator validation in this loop. Reloads may occur before the first prompt or after the last prompt, but at least one prompt must set response. The final response is the last prompt's returned text, even if a later reload changes session resources. When options contains an output property, its callback is awaited with {response, session}; otherwise the string is returned. The adapter's generic restricts custom output to JsonValue, while actual external createHarness normalization is a dependency boundary rather than locally implemented JSON validation (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:169-180; ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:246-259).
entries.interfaces: IceCodingAgentInput = string | Array<{type:'prompt', content:string}|{type:'reload'}>. Isolation layout: <tmp>/ice-eval-*/workspace, agent, sessions. Options: model selection, noTools, transformSystemPrompt(defaultPrompt), async or sync output({response, session}); output callback executes before snapshot/disposal/removal. Artifact 'runId' is the native session ID.
entries.dependency_text: AI-002 owns model runtime/catalog behavior; SESSION-028 owns SDK service/session construction and SESSION-035 owns resource reload. This entry adds the evaluation-specific construction and sequence policy without recounting those implementations.
entries.rust: AgentHarness::create genuinely builds a native harness over a supplied Session, providers, tools, settings and resource configuration (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:682-810). The complete inspected native harness_with_options helper constructs a FauxProvider, read/write/bash tools, InMemoryExecutionEnv and InMemorySessionStorage, then calls that constructor (rust:crates/ice-harness/tests/harness_run_e2e.rs:51-128). These are reusable isolated deterministic building blocks. They are not the application-session adapter that allocates real temporary project/agent/session directories, loads normal selected credentials, transforms the complete prompt, supports explicit reload steps and invokes an arbitrary JSON output projection. No native comparative eval wrapper was found in the bounded inventory.
entries.port: Build the eval adapter over the real application-session services and native harness, keeping model runtime resolution outside the temporary project settings. Allocate a scoped temporary root and explicit session storage, disable thinking for the baseline contract, forward tool policy, preserve transform-then-reload ordering and verify the initial extension set. Run prompt/reload steps in order and invoke the output projection while session/files still exist. Preserve the native deterministic in-memory helper for unit tests; use the real temporary project path when evaluating extension/resource authoring. Reuse SDK/reload implementations rather than replacing them with eval-specific mocks.
entries.priority_reason: Model comparisons require equivalent fresh application sessions and explicit reload behavior; native unit-test isolation alone does not provide that workflow.

entries.title: Eval cancellation, snapshot-before-disposal and cleanup error aggregation
entries.what: A run connects the evaluation signal to session abort, preserves the session JSONL while it still exists, attempts every cleanup operation, and reports cleanup failures without silently losing a primary run error.
entries.mechanism:
Abort is connected to the live session after construction and any initial prompt transformation. Cleanup then snapshots the session before disposing it and removing the temporary root. Failure reporting distinguishes the original run failure from later snapshot, disposal and removal errors.

The signal is checked before model/runtime work, after service creation, immediately after the abort listener is installed and before each prompt. The listener is once-only and memoizes evalSession.abort() in abortPromise. The inner finally removes the listener and awaits that promise if it was created. Initial transform/reload precedes listener installation; ordinary reload steps have no additional per-step throwIfAborted call. There is no final signal check after the output projection or usage collection. Therefore this source must not be described as a single enclosing cancellation race or as cancelling every setup phase immediately. An abortPromise rejection is an exception from the inner finally and becomes the caught run error, replacing any prompt/output exception already propagating through that finally (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:115-165; ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:169-210).

The protected try begins only after model lookup and mkdtemp succeed. Failures before that boundary reject directly; no created session exists there. Within the try, all failures become an outcome object. If a SessionManager exists, its session file path is checked and the existing UTF-8 file is read into artifact 'iceSessionJsonl'. Missing or nonexistent files produce no snapshot. Snapshot errors are collected, then session.dispose() is attempted synchronously, then rm(root,{recursive:true, force:true}) is awaited. Both later attempts occur even when an earlier cleanup operation failed. The source has no explicit ModelRuntime disposal operation (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:208-232).

If the run failed and cleanup did not, rethrow the original value unchanged. If both failed, throw AggregateError([originalError,...cleanupErrors], 'Agent run failed and cleanup also failed.'). On a successful run, one cleanup error is thrown directly and multiple errors produce AggregateError(cleanupErrors,'Agent cleanup failed.'). Only a fully successful outcome returns timings.totalMs, measured from before model setup through completed cleanup. Failed paths do not construct this successful timing payload. The four local unit suites do not exercise cancellation/disposal failure combinations; these are direct source contracts, not executed test results.
entries.interfaces: HarnessContext.signal: optional AbortSignal; at most one memoized session.abort() promise. Snapshot artifact key iceSessionJsonl stores unmodified UTF-8 native session JSONL before directory removal. Cleanup order: snapshot → dispose → recursive force rm; error order preserves original run error before cleanup errors. Successful timings.totalMs includes setup, prompts/reloads, output projection and cleanup.
entries.dependency_text: The application session supplies abort/dispose semantics through MISC-041's SDK prerequisites. MISC-044 consumes the saved snapshot; do not reverse that dependency or write the artifact after deleting the workspace.
entries.rust: Native AgentLane::abort cancels the active signal on the current lane and returns an AbortResult; it rejects for a closed harness, another active lane or no active run. It does not itself await completion. wait_for_idle is a distinct operation. close sets the closed flag and cancels the child scope; its own source does not implement an eval snapshot/remove transaction (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:4636-4666; rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:4882-4914; rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:2039-2047). These primitives are partial support, not equivalent to the eval adapter's memoized abort, snapshot and aggregated cleanup sequence.
entries.port: Use a scoped eval-run owner that records the primary outcome and independently attempts snapshot, session shutdown and temporary-root removal in that order. Map native cancellation to an explicit wait for the run/shutdown operation where needed, because native abort only signals. Preserve all cleanup errors and stable ordering in an aggregate error type. Keep the source's phase boundaries visible in compatibility behavior; any stronger cancellation guarantees during model initialization or reload should be documented and tested separately. Add future targeted failure-injection cases for snapshot failure, disposal failure, removal failure, abort rejection and a primary-plus-cleanup error.
entries.priority_reason: Evaluation failures must retain useful session evidence and reliably release temporary resources without concealing the original error.

entries.title: Strict prompt completion, normalized transcripts and evaluation usage
entries.what: The eval result contains a strict successful response, a normalized message/tool trace and session token/cost telemetry suitable for judges and paired comparisons.
entries.mechanism:
A prompt succeeds only when the newly appended messages include an assistant whose final stop reason is exactly 'stop' and the session exposes nonempty assistant text. The adapter then projects the complete session into evaluation events. It reports session-wide usage while retaining the initially selected model's identity and pricing gate.

promptAgent checks abort, records the current message count, awaits session.prompt(input), and searches the newly appended suffix backwards for an assistant. Missing assistant rejects. Any stopReason other than 'stop' rejects with errorMessage when non-nullish, otherwise 'Agent run ended with unexpected stop reason: <reason>.'. An explicitly empty errorMessage is retained by ??, not replaced. It obtains the response with getLastAssistantText() and rejects a falsy result; whitespace-only text remains truthy and is not trimmed here. The smoke scenario separately trims its own final assertion (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:90-107).

contentText returns a string unchanged or joins only text blocks with newline. For each user message, the transcript emits a user message event even if the extracted text is empty. For assistants it emits one nonempty combined text message, then one tool_call per toolCall content block in original tool-call order, with id/name and arguments delegated to external normalizeRecord. This groups all assistant text before its tool calls rather than preserving interleaving among original content blocks. Thinking and image blocks are not independent assistant trace events. A toolResult emits tool_result with toolCallId/name; all-text content becomes the combined string, otherwise the entire content array goes through external toJsonValue. Error results add error.message equal to the extracted text or 'Tool failed'.
