entries.title: Task-bound session/source artifacts and scoped attachment persistence
entries.what: Evaluation runs attach their native session JSONL and generated source to the explicit test task, then persist only attachments belonging to the reported run.
entries.mechanism:
Session snapshots are captured before workspace removal and registered on the actual Vitest task after each eval. The reporter persists selected session/source attachments into separate run-scoped directories. Run IDs are hashed for directory names, while the attachment basename is checked before writing.

ICE_SESSION_SNAPSHOT_ARTIFACT is the literal artifact key 'iceSessionJsonl'. recordEvalSessionArtifact receives an explicit Readonly<RunnerTestCase> and a run's artifact map. An undefined snapshot returns without validating runId; a present snapshot requires both runId and session to be strings or throws TypeError('Ice eval session artifact metadata is invalid.'). It records type '@zykairotis/ice-evals:session', the run ID and one attachment named session.jsonl with application/jsonl, UTF-8 body and bodyEncoding='utf-8'. The eval-only afterEach hook reads task.meta.harness?.run and calls this function when a run exists. It does not rely on an implicit currently running test during reporter execution (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/artifacts.ts:13-73; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/setup.ts:1-9).

recordEvalSourceArtifact records type '@zykairotis/ice-evals:source', a supplied runId and one SourceAttachment. Its TypeScript interface specifies name, contentType, string body and UTF-8 encoding, but this wrapper adds no runtime validation. Unique module-local symbols extend Vitest's TestArtifactRegistry for the two record types; the wire discriminator remains the string type.

persistEvalArtifactReferences walks artifacts in order and selects only these two types whose runId strictly equals the report run ID. It chooses sessions or sources by type. For each attachment it computes basename(name), rejects when that differs from the original name, creates <artifactDirectory>/<category>/<SHA-256(runId)> recursively with requested mode 0700, and writes the body as UTF-8 using requested mode 0600. The returned ordered references contain only {name, path}, with path relative to artifactDirectory. These checks use the host's basename semantics; they do not add a platform-independent path grammar or reject dot/empty basenames in advance. Such names can still fail at write time. Repeated same-category/run/name writes overwrite the same path and can yield repeated references; there is no content deduplication, exclusive-create option or rollback transaction. Mode arguments apply to creation and do not force a chmod of preexisting paths (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/artifacts.ts:87-112).

The direct suite was fully read: it checks explicit-task registration, run/type filtering, 64-hex run directories and exact persisted contents. It does not cover malformed attachment names, overwrite collisions or injected I/O failures. Session/source contents are retained unredacted by this helper, matching the README's description of prompts/responses/source/tool-output artifacts.

entries.title: Comparative harness tables, canonical input pairing and failure metadata
entries.what: A comparison declares one baseline and one or more candidates, repeats them in a stable order and attaches a deterministic input/repetition identity to every wrapped run, including recoverable partial failures.
entries.mechanism:
The table generates baseline-then-candidate rows for each repetition. Inputs are paired by a trimmed explicit string ID when available, otherwise by a hash of strict canonical JSON. Iteration metadata is attached before execution and merged into successful or externally attached partial runs.

Options accept either candidate or candidates with a baseline and optional repetitions. The implementation chooses the singular property when 'candidate' in options, otherwise uses the candidate array. Default repetitions is 1. validateOptions rejects a whitespace-only evalSet, zero candidates, duplicate exact harness.name values and repetitions that are not a positive safe integer. It does not trim stored evalSet/names or independently reject an empty harness name. Rows enumerate repetitions 1..N, with baseline first then candidates in declaration order. The builder does not randomize or schedule execution; callers use describe.for and may independently configure Vitest sequencing (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:114-128; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:157-193).

deriveInputKey first checks non-null, non-array object inputs with an 'id' property, including an inherited property. A nonempty trimmed string ID is returned directly and bypasses validation of all other input fields. Otherwise canonicalizeJson accepts null/string/boolean and finite numbers, dense arrays with an own property at every numeric index, and only Object.prototype/null-prototype objects. It rejects other primitive types, non-finite numbers, sparse arrays, cycles and non-plain object prototypes. Object.entries selects enumerable own string-keyed fields, sorts keys lexically with < and >, recursively canonicalizes values and reconstructs an object before JSON.stringify. The lexical comparison is JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit order. Because the sorted entries are reconstructed as an ordinary object, canonical array-index keys from '0' through '4294967294' serialize first in numeric order, followed by the other sorted string keys; the final JSON text is not a generic all-keys-lexicographic encoding. The hash also inherits JSON.stringify number/string encoding, including -0 becoming 0. The WeakSet tracks ancestors and deletes on return, so repeated noncyclic object references are allowed. SHA-256 of that canonical JSON string becomes a lower-case hex input key. The final group key is JSON.stringify([inputKey, repetition]); explicit IDs and hash keys share the same string namespace (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:66-112).

Each wrapper sets artifact 'vitestEvalsHarnessIteration' before calling the underlying harness. The artifact is {schemaVersion:1, evalSet, groupKey, harness, baseline, candidates, repetition}. On success, it mutates run.artifacts by merging context.artifacts, then existing run.artifacts, then the authoritative iteration value. On failure it asks external getHarnessRunFromError for a partial run; when present it performs the same merge and rethrows through attachHarnessRunToError. Errors without an attached run are rethrown unchanged. A group-key error happens before the artifact is set (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:130-155).

The parser is intentionally less strict than the table builder: it requires a non-array object, schemaVersion===1, the named string fields, an array of string candidate names and typeof repetition==='number'. It does not require finite/positive/integer repetition, nonempty strings, unique candidates or baseline/harness membership. The direct tests cover canonical key order, trimmed IDs, array order, unsupported/sparse/cyclic inputs, row order, singular candidate and success metadata. They do not assert all builder/parser validation branches or the partial-error attachment path.

entries.title: Per-test run index, observation extraction and interrupted-run reporting
entries.what: The eval reporter appends a compact index for each completed harness-bearing test and derives comparison observations from explicit iteration metadata and judge scores.
entries.mechanism:
A per-test callback persists attachments and appends a JSONL run record when an artifact directory is configured. A separate end-of-run pass derives observations from test metadata and prints the paired comparison report. An interrupted run suppresses that aggregate comparison without erasing already written per-test records.

appendHarnessRunReport trims ICE_EVAL_ARTIFACT_DIR and returns when absent or empty. Unlike the runner, this function does not resolve the value relative to the eval package root. It requires test.meta().harness and external isHarnessRun(harness.run). A string run.artifacts.runId is retained, including an empty string; otherwise a UUID is generated. Metadata copies every run artifact except runId and iceSessionJsonl. The record is schemaVersion1 with runId; test{id, file:relativeModuleId, name, fullName, status}; harness name; usage; optional timings; nonempty errors; persisted attachment references; and nonempty metadata. It does not directly serialize the output, normalized transcript or test.meta().eval.avgScore into this local index (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:14-44).

Attachment persistence happens before creating the root and appending runs.jsonl. The root is requested recursively with mode 0700; appendFile uses UTF-8, flag'a' and mode 0600. There is no local index deduplication, file lock, whole-record transaction with attachments, or recovery rollback. I/O errors propagate from the awaited callback; attachments may exist even when the later index append fails. Other reporters may emit their own formats, but those external formats are not inferred here (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:42-50; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:96-98).

collectHarnessObservations enumerates every module's allTests, requires a recognized harness run and a successfully parsed vitestEvalsHarnessIteration artifact, and copies evalSet/groupKey/harness/baseline/candidates/repetition. Pairing uses module.relativeModuleId and test.name, not fullName. avgScore and estimatedCostUsd are accepted only when typeof number and finite. totalTokens and totalMs are copied when not undefined; the summary later rejects non-finite metric pairs. If run.errors is nonempty, outcome is errored even when a judge score exists. Otherwise a finite judge score creates a scored observation regardless of the Vitest result state. Without a score, passed becomes unscored, failed becomes errored, and other test states pass through. A failed hard assertion with an existing finite score and no harness-run error is therefore still scored for this comparison, although Vitest may fail the test (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:53-87).

onInit stores the Vitest logger. onTestRunEnd ignores its serialized-error argument; reason==='interrupted' prints the unavailable message and returns. Other end reasons summarize and format the collected observations, printing only nonempty output. Tests that never produced a recognized harness run or iteration artifact are not synthesized into observations; a missing counterpart can only be diagnosed where another observed run declares the comparison. The local inventory has no dedicated reporter unit suite, so these branches are source-read only.

Environment ICE_EVAL_ARTIFACT_DIR. runs.jsonl schemaVersion1 fields: runId, test, harness, usage, timings?, errors?, artifacts, metadata?. Test metadata inputs harness.run and eval.avgScore. Outcome precedence: harness errors → finite score → mapped test state. Interrupted message: 'Eval comparisons unavailable: test run interrupted.'.

entries.title: Paired correctness lift, telemetry availability and diagnostic terminal summaries
entries.what: Comparison summaries pair each declared candidate only with its baseline, calculate correctness separately from efficiency, and expose missing/duplicate/error observations instead of filling them with zero.
entries.mechanism:
The summary uses matched observations for the same file, test name, input key and repetition. Correctness is the difference in pass rates, while tokens, latency and estimated cost are separate paired metrics. Missing scores or telemetry remain unavailable and contribute explicit coverage or diagnostics.

groupObservations groups first by evalSet. The first observation fixes that set's baseline; later conflicting baseline declarations are not validated. Candidate names are unioned, retaining their smallest observed declaration index. Each group key is JSON.stringify([file,testName,groupKey]); the stored repetition and other group labels come from the first observation, so repetition only affects grouping independently when already encoded by the table's groupKey. Runs with the same file, leaf test.name and input key can collide even if their fullName differs. Observations are stored as arrays per harness, retaining duplicates. Candidates sort by retained index then localeCompare name; eval sets sort by localeCompare, groups by groupKey then repetition (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:112-161).

Every group and declared harness is diagnosed once with this precedence: zero observations→missing-observation; more than one→duplicate-observation; one errored→harness-error; one unscored→missing-score; one other non-scored outcome→unscorable-outcome. Diagnostics are shared across all candidate comparisons and finally sort by evalSet, file, groupKey, repetition, harness; they are not duplicated for each pair. Each candidate is paired only with the declared baseline, and only groups with exactly one observation for each side become candidate pairs. totalPairs is all groups in the eval set, including groups with missing or duplicate data (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:164-210; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:284-328).

Correctness includes a pair only when both outcomes are scored. A score>=1 is a pass; no rounding, clamping or fractional-credit pass threshold is substituted. Baseline/candidate wins mean only one side passes; ties mean both pass or both fail. Pass rates divide by eligiblePairs; zero eligible pairs yields null rates and lift. Lift is candidateRate-baselineRate, rounded through Number(difference.toPrecision(15)). The public summary function itself does not revalidate score finiteness; its normal reporter caller filters scores under MISC-046. Metrics likewise require two scored observations and two defined finite values, independently for totalTokens, totalMs, estimatedCostUsd. Negative finite values are not rejected by this helper. It computes each side's mean over that metric's eligible pairs and the same 15-significant-digit candidate-minus-baseline difference. No value is imputed for missing telemetry, and no confidence interval or significance test is computed (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:104-110; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:212-281).

Formatting returns empty when every eval set has no comparisons, even if a manually supplied report has diagnostics. Otherwise it prints 'Eval Comparisons', set names, right-aligned 9-character labels, baseline and candidate names and correctness eligible/total pair counts. Pass rates use one decimal percent and lift uses signed one-decimal percentage points. Tokens and milliseconds use one decimal; estimated USD uses four. Positive correctness is green, negative correctness red; lower efficiency metrics are green, higher red; zero deltas gray and unavailable values yellow. Metric coverage is appended only for a nonzero eligible count that differs from correctness eligiblePairs; a wholly unavailable metric has no separate zero-pair suffix. Incomplete observations follow with reason, file/testName, repetition, harness. Styling uses Node styleText; terminal color emission policy is not reimplemented locally (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:330-438).

The full direct suite covers correctness versus efficiency, missing observations/telemetry, file separation, harness-error and unscored exclusion, baseline-only candidate comparisons, declared missing harnesses, deduplicated diagnostics and terminal strings. These assertions were inspected only; no model/test execution or statistical result was produced.

entries.title: Built-in smoke and extension-authoring evaluation scenarios
entries.what: The shipped suites exercise a real selected model and a create/reload/use extension workflow, comparing prompt variants with an all-or-nothing behavioral judge while retaining source/session evidence.
entries.mechanism:
The smoke suite checks one no-tools answer and basic model telemetry. The extension suite compares two system-prompt variants on the same two-prompt workflow with an intervening resource reload. Its judge records task correctness, while hard assertions protect the intended prompt-treatment setup.

The smoke harness uses noTools='all' and the default harness/model selection. It asks for the capital of France, requires output.trim()==='Paris', result.errors===[], usage.provider/model equal the ICE_PROVIDER/ICE_MODEL environment values and totalTokens>0. It supplies no iteration table or judge, so the local comparison collector ignores it, though its recognized harness run can still be indexed. The runner may launch with no model defaults, but executing this shipped default-model smoke test still fails selection unless defaults exist; the no-default allowance applies when selected harnesses configure their own model (ice:packages/evals/src/smoke.eval.ts:1-18; ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:49-63).

createExtensionAuthoringHarness projects the response, markers for Guidelines and ICE documentation in the effective system prompt, resource-loader errors, each loaded extension path/tool-name list and the UTF-8 source at <session cwd>/.ice/extensions/hello.ts when it exists. The baseline 'system-prompt-without-docs' truncates the default prompt at the first '\nGuidelines:\n' and throws if absent. Candidate 'default-system-prompt' removes the last '\nCurrent working directory: ' suffix and throws if absent. The two transforms are not arbitrary whole-section parsers; they use these exact string markers and slices. evalHarnessTable uses its default one repetition with baseline then candidate (ice:packages/evals/src/extensions.eval.ts:18-51; ice:packages/evals/src/extensions.eval.ts:100-103).

Both runs ask the model to create a hello tool accepting a name, reload the session, then ask it to call the tool for Bob and respond with exactly the greeting. The source path is a fixed expected hello.ts even though the first prompt does not explicitly name that file. The judge fails when that source is unavailable. It extracts imports with a regex matching from/import followed by whitespace and a quoted specifier; this is not a TypeScript parser and does not inspect dynamic import(...) forms. It requires a canonical @zykairotis/ice-coding-agent import, rejects matched @mariozechner/* or @sinclair/typebox* imports, requires zero loader errors and a loaded 'hello' tool, and requires a normalized successful call named hello with arguments.name==='Bob' and result==='Hello, Bob!'. Final response must equal 'Hello, Bob!' exactly without trimming. All conditions must pass for score 1; otherwise score 0 with semicolon-joined rationale metadata (ice:packages/evals/src/extensions.eval.ts:53-98).

describeEval receives that judge and judgeThreshold:null, expressing observational scoring rather than a score threshold gate. The test records hello.ts as a text/typescript UTF-8 source artifact when source exists, requiring a string runId first. It then hard-asserts that Guidelines/documentation markers match whether the harness name is 'default-system-prompt'. The README directs comparative suites to use judges for correctness and hard assertions only for setup/infrastructure invariants; it states that expect.soft still fails a test. That external framework behavior is not independently executed here. Four local unit suites test helper contracts, while the two *.eval.ts files are model-backed scenarios whose outcomes remain unverified.
